definition_zh: 爱好者；恋人；情人；热爱者
definition_en: a person who loves someone romantically; also a person who greatly enjoys a particular activity or subject
core_image: 一个人把一束花轻轻放进另一双手里，目光只停在对方脸上
scene: 黄昏的街角，一个人把写好的信折好，塞进对方家的门缝，随后快步走开。The lover waited by the fountain every evening, holding a small red box.
sceneCN: 这里 lover 是「恋人、情人」（第 2 个义项：恋爱对象）；句意为恋人每晚都等在喷泉边，手里拿着一个小红盒。画面里可认出街角、折好的信与喷泉。

pos.zh: 爱好者；恋人；情人；热爱者

derivatives.zh: 构成 lover 的名词基础，义为「爱；爱情」
由 love 加形容词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「可爱的；美好的」
由 love 加后缀 -able 构成，义为「惹人喜爱的」

senses.title: A person who greatly enjoys an activity or subject
senses.definition: a person who takes great interest and pleasure in a particular activity, subject or object
senses.definitionCN: 对某项活动、学科或事物有浓厚兴趣并从中获得乐趣的人
senses.example: She is a lifelong music lover who never misses a concert.
senses.exampleCN: 她是一辈子的音乐爱好者，从不错过任何一场音乐会。
senses.why: The verb love means to hold something dear, and the person suffix -er turns that feeling into an identity, so anyone who loves a thing deeply can be called its lover.
senses.whyCN: 动词 love 表示珍视某物，表示「人」的后缀 -er 把这种感情变成一种身份，所以任何深爱某事物的人都可以被称为它的 lover。

senses.title: A person someone is in a romantic relationship with
senses.definition: a person with whom someone has a romantic and usually sexual relationship
senses.definitionCN: 与某人处于恋爱关系、通常也包含性关系的人
senses.example: He wrote a letter to his lover before leaving the city.
senses.exampleCN: 离开这座城市之前，他给恋人写了一封信。
senses.why: Romantic love is the most intense form of holding someone dear, so the same person suffix naturally names the one who receives that love rather than the one who only feels it.
senses.whyCN: 恋爱是「珍视某人」最强烈的一种形式，于是同一个表示人的后缀自然指接受这份爱的那个人，而不只是付出爱的人。

senses.title: A person in a secret or extramarital sexual relationship
senses.definition: a person who has a sexual relationship with someone who is married to another person or already has a partner
senses.definitionCN: 与已婚者或已有伴侣者保持性关系的人；婚外情人
senses.example: The novel opens with a married man meeting his lover in a small hotel.
senses.exampleCN: 小说一开头，一个已婚男子在一家小旅馆与情人见面。
senses.why: Because the romantic sense is strong, the word takes on a discreet and often disapproving colour when the relationship has to be hidden from a spouse.
senses.whyCN: 因为恋爱义很强烈，当这种关系必须对配偶隐瞒时，这个词就带上隐秘、常含贬义的色彩，用来指婚外情人。

intro.en: Lover is love plus the person suffix -er; love itself goes back to an Old English word for deep affection.
intro.cn: lover 是 love 加表示「人」的后缀 -er；love 本身可追溯到古英语中表示深厚感情的词。

items.en: Old English lufu named love as a feeling, and the verb lufian meant to love or to hold dear.
items.cn: 古英语 lufu 指「爱」这种感情，动词 lufian 意为爱、珍视。

items.en: The reconstructed ancestor is lubō, a form rebuilt by comparing related Germanic languages rather than found in writing.
items.cn: 其重构祖形为 lubō，这一形式是通过比较相关日耳曼语言重建出来的，并非见于书面记录。

items.en: Middle English joined love with -er and produced lover, a person who loves or is loved.
items.cn: 中古英语把 love 与 -er 结合，造出 lover，指爱着别人或被爱的人。

items.en: The word covered both the devoted admirer of an art and the partner in a romance, and context decided which one was meant.
items.cn: 这个词同时指对某门艺术痴迷的爱好者和恋爱中的伴侣，具体指哪一个由上下文决定。

items.en: Modern English keeps the romantic sense at the centre, while compounds such as music lover and nature lover preserve the older sense of devoted admirer.
items.cn: 现代英语以恋爱义为中心，而 music lover、nature lover 这类复合词保留了「痴迷的爱好者」这一较早含义。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the love family and its derived forms; the near-meaning group collects other words for people who love, admire or are loved.
note.cn: 形近组收 love 词族及其派生形式；近义组收其他表示爱慕、欣赏或被爱的人称。

entries.definition: A deep feeling of affection for a person or thing.
entries.definitionCN: 对人或事物怀有的深厚感情；爱。

entries.definition: Pleasing and attractive; built from love with -ly.
entries.definitionCN: 讨人喜欢、好看的；由 love 加 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: Easy to love because of a warm character.
entries.definitionCN: 因性格温暖而容易让人喜爱的。

entries.definition: Greatly loved, often used of a person who is dear to many.
entries.definitionCN: 深受爱戴的，常形容被众人珍视的人。

entries.definition: A person who likes, respects or loves someone, sometimes secretly.
entries.definitionCN: 喜欢、敬重或爱慕某人的人，有时是暗中的。

entries.definition: A person strongly devoted to a hobby, cause or person.
entries.definitionCN: 对某项爱好、事业或某人极为投入的人。

entries.definition: A person with eager and active interest in a subject.
entries.definitionCN: 对某一主题怀有热切而积极兴趣的人。

entries.definition: A person one loves romantically; an affectionate form of address.
entries.definitionCN: 所爱的恋人；也用作亲昵称呼。

normalIntro.en: The word is a transparent build from love and the person suffix -er, so its hooks come from the feeling, the suffix and the compounds it forms.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词由 love 与表示人的后缀 -er 清楚构成，记忆钩子来自这份感情、这个后缀以及它组成的复合词。

normal.en: Lover is love plus -er, so the word literally means the one who loves.
normal.cn: lover 是 love 加 -er，字面意思就是「爱的那个人」。

normal.en: The plural is lovers, made by adding s to the singular.
normal.cn: 复数是 lovers，直接在单数后加 s。

normal.en: Music lover and nature lover are fixed compounds that keep the sense of devoted admirer.
normal.cn: music lover 与 nature lover 是固定复合词，保留了「痴迷的爱好者」这层意思。

normal.en: Beloved adds the prefix be- to loved, giving the sense of being greatly loved.
normal.cn: beloved 在 loved 前加前缀 be-，表示「深受爱戴的」。

normal.en: Lover names a person, while love names the feeling or the person addressed, so the two words split the roles.
normal.cn: lover 指人，love 指感情或对对方的称呼，两个词分担了不同角色。

abstract.en: A suffix that turns a feeling into a person shows how English builds identities out of emotions.
abstract.cn: 一个把感情变成人的后缀，说明英语会用情感来构造身份。

abstract.en: The same word can name a concert fan and a secret partner, because both are defined by what they love.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既能指音乐会的粉丝，也能指秘密情人，因为两者都由「爱什么」来定义。

abstract.en: Lover reminds us that love is not only felt inside but always points at someone or something outside.
abstract.cn: lover 提醒人：爱不只是在心里感受，它总是指向外的某个人或某样东西。

examples.en: She is a lifelong music lover who never misses a concert.
examples.cn: 她是一辈子的音乐爱好者，从不错过任何一场音乐会。

examples.en: He wrote a letter to his lover before leaving the city.
examples.cn: 离开这座城市之前，他给恋人写了一封信。

examples.en: The garden was planted by two nature lovers who met at a birdwatching club.
examples.cn: 这座花园是两位在观鸟俱乐部相识的自然爱好者种下的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「拉我」——恋爱时总想拉住对方的手，记住 lover 是恋人。

root: love（古英语 lufu，爱）加表示「人」的后缀 -er；lufu 一般认为来自原始日耳曼语 lubō，属日耳曼语族词汇，没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a person defined by love; the senses divide into the devoted admirer, the romantic partner and the hidden partner.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是由「爱」来定义的人；义项分出痴迷的爱好者、恋爱对象，以及隐秘的情人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one person placing a bunch of flowers into another pair of hands, eyes fixed on the other face.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人把一束花放进另一双手里，目光只停在对方脸上。

branches.cn: 坐满熟记每首歌的听众的音乐厅

branches.en: a gardener who names every bird that visits

branches.en: a person whose love is both a hobby and a bond
branches.cn: 既是爱好又是羁绊的爱

intro.en: Lover is built from a Germanic noun of affection and an English person suffix, and the same root later forms adjectives and a prefixed participle.
intro.cn: lover 由日耳曼语中表示感情的名词与英语表示人的后缀构成，同一词根后来又造出形容词和带前缀的分词。

latinIntro.en: Love is a Germanic word, so lover has no reliable Latin cognate recorded for it.
latinIntro.cn: love 是日耳曼语词，因此 lover 没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.exampleCN: 古英语 lufu 是 modern love 背后的名词。

items.example: Love can be quiet and steady rather than dramatic.
items.exampleCN: 爱可以安静而稳定，不必轰轰烈烈。

definition_zh: 低的；矮的；低落的；低声的；低点；低水平
definition_en: not high or tall; below the usual level, amount or value; also sad, quiet or deep in sound, and a lowest point
core_image: 一只手掌压向地面，把一根横杆缓缓降到几乎贴着泥土的位置
scene: 傍晚的球场边，一个孩子把球贴着草地滚出去，球一路几乎不离开泥土。The ball stayed low and skimmed over the wet grass.
sceneCN: 这里 low 是「低的、贴近地面的」（第 1 个义项：高度低）；句意为球一直贴着地面，从湿草上滑过去。画面里可认出球场边、草地与滚动的球。

pos.zh: 低的；矮的；低落的；低声的

derivatives.zh: low 的比较级形式兼作动词，义为「降低；放下」
由 low 加形容词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「卑微的；地位低的」
由前缀 be- 与 low 构成，义为「在……下面；低于」
由 low 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「低；低落」

senses.title: Not high in height or position
senses.definition: having a small distance from the top to the ground, or standing near the ground
senses.definitionCN: 从顶部到地面的距离小，或位置接近地面的
senses.example: The shelf is low enough for a child to reach.
senses.exampleCN: 这个架子很低，孩子够得着。
senses.why: The oldest use describes a body or object near the ground, so lowness begins as a physical distance rather than a value.
senses.whyCN: 最早的用法描述人或物贴近地面的位置，所以「低」首先是一种空间距离，而不是价值判断。

senses.title: Below the usual level or amount
senses.definition: less than the normal, expected or average amount, level or value
senses.definitionCN: 低于正常、预期或平均的数量、水平或数值
senses.example: The river is unusually low this summer.
senses.exampleCN: 今年夏天这条河的水位异常低。
senses.why: Once the word can measure height, it can measure any scale, so a low river or a low price simply sits far down its own scale.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词能度量高度，就能度量任何尺度，于是低水位、低价格只是在自己的尺度上位置很靠下。

senses.title: Sad, weak or without energy
senses.definition: feeling unhappy, tired or without hope and energy
senses.definitionCN: 感到不快、疲惫，或缺少希望与精力
senses.example: He felt low for weeks after moving to the new city.
senses.exampleCN: 搬到新城市后，他情绪低落了几个星期。
senses.why: A low position is close to the ground, and English links that downward picture with a lowered spirit, so the word moves from space to mood.
senses.whyCN: 低的位置贴近地面，英语把这幅向下的画面与低落的精神联系起来，于是词义从空间转到情绪。

senses.title: Soft in volume or deep in pitch
senses.definition: produced quietly, or having a deep pitch rather than a high one
senses.definitionCN: 以较小的音量发出，或音调低沉而不高尖的
senses.example: She answered in a low voice so the others would not hear.
senses.exampleCN: 她低声回答，免得别人听见。
senses.why: A deep note sits at the bottom of the scale and a quiet voice carries less force, so both are heard as a kind of downward position.
senses.whyCN: 低沉的音处在音阶底部，轻声说话的力量也更小，两者听起来都像一种向下的位置。

senses.title: A low point, level or area
senses.definition: a point or level that is the lowest reached, or an area of low pressure in weather
senses.definitionCN: 所达到的最低点或最低水平，也指天气图上气压较低的区域
senses.example: Sales reached a new low in the winter.
senses.exampleCN: 冬季销售额跌到了新的低点。
senses.why: Because the adjective can measure any scale, English turns it into a noun for the bottom value itself, and weather writers use it for low pressure.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个形容词能度量各种尺度，英语就把它变成名词，指最低的那个数值本身，气象作者又用它指低气压。

intro.en: Low is an Old English adjective for being near the ground; it later spread from height to amounts, mood and sound.
intro.cn: low 是古英语中表示贴近地面的形容词，后来从高度扩展到数量、情绪与声音。

items.en: The adjective lāh meant low or humble, and it could describe both the ground and a person's rank.
items.cn: 形容词 lāh 意为低的、卑微的，既能形容地面，也能形容人的地位。

items.en: The reconstructed form is lauha-, rebuilt from related Germanic words such as Dutch laag.
items.cn: 其重构形式为 lauha-，是通过荷兰语 laag 等相关日耳曼词重建出来的。

items.en: Middle English lowe kept the physical sense and began to describe prices, voices and spirits.
items.cn: 中古英语的 lowe 保留物理义，并开始形容价格、嗓音与情绪。

items.en: Writers extended the word to any scale that could be measured, from income to temperature.
items.cn: 作家把这个词扩展到任何可度量的尺度，从收入到温度。

items.en: Modern English uses low for height, level, mood and voice, and as a noun for the lowest point.
items.cn: 现代英语用 low 指高度、水平、情绪与嗓音，也用作名词指最低点。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the low family and a spelling neighbour; the near-meaning group collects words for small height, small depth and low rank.
note.cn: 形近组收 low 词族与一个拼写相近的词；近义组收表示高度小、深度小与地位低的词。

entries.definition: The comparative of low, also a verb meaning to bring down.
entries.definitionCN: low 的比较级，也可作动词表示降低。

entries.definition: Humble in rank or position; built from low with -ly.
entries.definitionCN: 地位或身份卑微的；由 low 加 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: Under or lower than something, built with be- and low.
entries.definitionCN: 在……下面或低于某物，由 be- 与 low 构成。

entries.definition: Not fast; only the spelling and rhyme are close, and the origin is different.
entries.definitionCN: 缓慢的；只是拼写与读音和 low 相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: Having little height when said of a person or thing.
entries.definitionCN: 形容人或物时表示个子矮、高度小。

entries.definition: Not deep, with little distance from top to bottom.
entries.definitionCN: 不深的，从顶到底距离很小。

entries.definition: Low in rank or importance, without pride.
entries.definitionCN: 地位或重要性低，不骄傲。

entries.definition: Making little or no sound.
entries.definitionCN: 发出很少声音或没有声音的。

entries.definition: Going far down from the top or surface.
entries.definitionCN: 从顶部或表面向下延伸很深的。

normalIntro.en: The word has been about being near the ground since Old English, and its family keeps returning to downward position, lower value and lowered feeling.
normalIntro.cn: 自古英语起这个词就表示贴近地面，同族词反复回到向下的位置、更低的值与低落的情绪。

normal.en: Old English lāh already meant low, so the word has kept its shape and sense for a very long time.
normal.cn: 古英语 lāh 已经表示低，所以这个词的形态与含义都保持了很长时间。

normal.en: The comparative is lower and the superlative is lowest, both made with the regular endings.
normal.cn: 比较级是 lower，最高级是 lowest，都用规则词尾构成。

normal.en: Below is be- plus low, literally at a lower place than something.
normal.cn: below 是 be- 加 low，字面就是「处于比某物更低的位置」。

normal.en: Low season names the quiet months of a trade, when prices and crowds are at their lowest.
normal.cn: low season 指行业的淡季，此时价格与客流都处在最低。

normal.en: Low point is a fixed phrase for the worst or weakest moment of a period.
normal.cn: low point 是固定说法，指一段时期里最糟或最弱的时刻。

abstract.en: A word that starts as a measurement of height ends up measuring mood, price and sound, because English reads downward as less.
abstract.cn: 一个从高度测量开始的词，最后用来测量情绪、价格与声音，因为英语把「向下」读作「更少」。

abstract.en: The same low note and low mood share a shape: both are felt as sinking rather than rising.
abstract.cn: 低沉的音与低落的情绪共享一种形状：两者都被感觉为下沉而不是上升。

abstract.en: A low point is only meaningful against a scale, which is why the word always implies something higher above it.
abstract.cn: 低点只有相对某个尺度才有意义，所以这个词总暗示着上方还有更高的东西。

examples.en: The shelf is low enough for a child to reach.
examples.cn: 这个架子很低，孩子够得着。

examples.en: The river is unusually low this summer.
examples.cn: 今年夏天这条河的水位异常低。

examples.en: She answered in a low voice so the others would not hear.
examples.cn: 她低声回答，免得别人听见。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a position near the ground; the senses then measure level, mood, sound and finally the lowest point itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是贴近地面的位置；义项随后度量水平、情绪、声音，最后指最低点本身。

intro.en: Low is a short Germanic adjective that English has turned into comparison, a verb, a compound and a noun.
intro.cn: low 是一个简短的日耳曼语形容词，英语把它发展出比较级、动词、复合词与名词用法。

latinIntro.en: Low belongs to the Germanic family, so it has no reliable Latin cognate.

items.example: Old English lāh described both the ground and a person's rank.
items.exampleCN: 古英语 lāh 既形容地面，也形容人的地位。

items.meaning: near the ground or below a level
items.example: The wall was low enough to look over.

items.meaning: more low; also to bring down
items.example: The sun sank lower behind the hills.

items.example: The lake reaches its lowest level in autumn.

definition_zh: 忠诚的；忠实的（对人、团体或事业）；忠贞的（对伴侣与誓言）；效忠的（对君主或国家）；长期支持的（顾客与读者）；矢志不渝的（对原则）；制度内批评而仍忠于整体的
definition_en: faithful to a person, group, cause or duty, and unwilling to abandon it even when doing so would be easier or more profitable
core_image: 老街照相馆的冲洗师，在师父去世、店面几经转手之后，仍每天早晨开门，把褪色的招牌擦一遍，再把师父的合影摆回柜台原位
scene: 老街上的照相馆换过三任房东，冲洗师仍每天早晨拉起卷帘门，把褪色的招牌擦干净，再把师父留下的合影摆回柜台原位。He stayed loyal to the little studio long after its founder had died and the building had changed hands.
sceneCN: 这里 loyal 形容「对某个人或某个地方长期不离不弃的忠诚」（第 1 个义项：对某人在困境中仍不背弃）；句意为创办人去世、楼宇数次转手之后，他仍守着这间小照相馆。可辨识物件：褪色的招牌、师父的合影相框、清晨拉起的卷帘门、挂在腰间的旧钥匙；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 忠诚的；忠实的；忠贞的；效忠的；矢志不渝的

senses.title: Faithful to a person
senses.definition: staying attached to a friend, partner or leader and refusing to abandon them when loyalty becomes costly
senses.definitionCN: 对朋友、伴侣或领导者保持依恋，即使忠诚要付出代价也不离弃
senses.example: She stayed loyal to her first coach after a richer club offered her a place.
senses.exampleCN: 更有钱的俱乐部给了她一个位置之后，她仍忠于最初的教练。
senses.why: The Latin source described someone who keeps the law, and keeping faith with a person grew out of that legal idea of standing by an obligation.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁来源形容守法的人，而「对人守信」正是从「守着一项义务」这一法律观念里长出来的。

senses.title: Faithful to a group or cause
senses.definition: giving steady support to a team, party, school or cause over many years
senses.definitionCN: 多年间稳定地支持某个球队、党派、学校或事业
senses.example: He has been loyal to the same football club since he was six.
senses.exampleCN: 他从六岁起就忠于同一家足球俱乐部。
senses.why: The sworn bond to a lord widened into any body one chooses to belong to.
senses.whyCN: 对领主宣誓的纽带，扩展成了对任何自己选择归属的团体的纽带。

senses.title: True to a promise or duty
senses.definition: keeping the terms of an oath, a vow or a post even when no one is watching
senses.definitionCN: 即使无人监督，也遵守誓言、婚誓或职位的条款
senses.example: The nurse was loyal to her oath and never repeated what she had seen in the ward.
senses.exampleCN: 那名护士忠于自己的誓词，从未把病房里看到的事说出去。
senses.why: Medieval usage applied the lawful man to anyone who kept his word, which is the bridge from law to faithfulness.
senses.whyCN: 中世纪用法把这个「守法之人」用在任何守信者身上，这正是从法律通往忠贞的桥。

senses.title: A customer who keeps coming back
senses.definition: in business, describing a customer or reader who returns to the same shop, paper or brand year after year
senses.definitionCN: 商业用语，形容年复一年回到同一家店、同一份报纸或同一个品牌的顾客或读者
senses.example: The bookshop has a small but loyal readership that has outlasted three owners.
senses.exampleCN: 这家书店的读者不多却忠实，熬过了三任店主。
senses.why: Modern trade borrowed the moral word to measure attachment that survives better offers.
senses.whyCN: 现代商业借用了这个道德词，用来衡量那种在更优条件面前仍然留存的依恋。

senses.title: Holding to a principle
senses.definition: remaining faithful to a belief, habit or memory that one has inherited or chosen
senses.definitionCN: 对自己继承或选定的信念、习惯或记忆保持忠实
senses.example: He remained loyal to the principles his father had taught him, even when they cost him a promotion.
senses.exampleCN: 他始终忠于父亲教给他的原则，即便这些原则让他失去了升职机会。
senses.why: Once faithfulness needs no second person, it attaches to ideas, and the word describes consistency of belief.
senses.whyCN: 当忠贞不再需要另一个对象时，它就附着在观念上，这个词便描述信念的一贯。

senses.title: Faithful in love
senses.definition: remaining true to a partner and refusing the attentions of others
senses.definitionCN: 对伴侣保持忠实，拒绝他人的示好
senses.example: They promised to remain loyal to each other through two years of living in different countries.
senses.exampleCN: 他们答应在分居两国的两年里彼此忠贞。
senses.why: The oldest personal sense comes from courtly writing, where faithfulness was proved by distance and temptation.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的个人义项来自宫廷文学，那里的忠贞要靠距离与诱惑来证明。

senses.title: Sworn to a sovereign or state
senses.definition: in political and military usage, staying on the side of a crown, government or flag during conflict
senses.definitionCN: 政治与军事用语，指冲突中仍站在王室、政府或旗帜一边
senses.example: The regiment stayed loyal to the crown even after half the capital had changed sides.
senses.exampleCN: 即便半个首都都已倒向另一方，这个团仍效忠王室。
senses.why: This is the feudal core of the word: a sworn man bound to a lord by oath rather than by opinion.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词的封建内核：宣誓者靠誓言而非主张绑定于领主。

senses.title: Loyal opposition
senses.definition: in parliamentary language, describing criticism offered from inside the system by those who do not wish to overthrow it
senses.definitionCN: 议会用语，指体制内部提出批评、却不希望推翻体制的人所做的批评
senses.example: A loyal opposition attacks the minister's policy without attacking the state itself.
senses.exampleCN: 忠诚的反对派抨击部长的政策，却不攻击国家本身。
senses.why: The word can even cover sharp criticism, which shows that loyalty is owed to the whole rather than to a person's wishes.
senses.whyCN: 这个词甚至能涵盖尖锐批评，可见忠诚所向是整体，而不是某人的意愿。

intro.en: Loyal comes from Old French loial, from Latin legalis 'of the law', from lex 'law'. English legal is the same Latin word borrowed directly and much later, so loyal and legal are doublets: one source, two arrivals.
intro.cn: loyal 来自古法语 loial，源头是拉丁 legalis「法律的」，再上溯为 lex「法律」。同一个拉丁词后来又被直接借入英语，成为表示「法律的」的那个形容词，因此本词与它属同一来源的两次借入。

items.en: Lex meant law or statute. Source uncertain: no agreed origin exists, and a link with legere 'to gather, read' is a hypothesis rather than a settled derivation.
items.cn: lex 意为法律、法令。来源不确定：没有公认的起源；一般认为它与 legere「收集、读」有关，但这只是假说，不是已证实的派生。

items.en: Legalis meant 'belonging to the law'. Medieval usage also applied it to a person who keeps the law, and from there to one who keeps faith.
items.cn: legalis 意为「属于法律的」。中世纪用法也用它形容守法的人，进而形容守信的人。

items.en: Old French changed legalis into loial, and the sense moved from lawful to faithful, above all faithful to a lord.
items.cn: 古法语把 legalis 变成 loial，词义也从「合法的」转为「忠实的」，尤其指对领主忠实。

items.en: English borrowed the adjective around the fifteenth century for the bond between a sworn follower and his lord; the exact first date is not settled, and the modern senses spread outward from that bond.
items.cn: 英语大约在十五世纪借入这个形容词，用于宣誓的追随者与领主之间的纽带；确切首见年代并无定论，现代各个义项都是从那一条纽带向外扩展的。

items.en: Legalis was borrowed a second time, directly and with its meaning intact, giving English legal; the two words now share a source but not a sense.
items.cn: legalis 后来又被直接借入一次，词义保持原样，成为表示「法律的」的那个英语形容词；这两个词如今共享来源，却不共享词义。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin and first date): the root of lex has no agreed explanation, the legere connection remains a suggestion, and any Indo-European form proposed for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源与首见年代）：lex 的词根没有公认解释；与 legere 的关联仍只是推测；凡为其提出的印欧形式均属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same Latin law noun, including the doublet that arrived by the direct route, plus one look-alike from an unrelated royal stem; group two holds adjectives of attachment that differ in basis and warmth.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁「法律」名词的词，包括沿直接借入路线到达的那个双重借入词，以及一个词形相近却出自无关「王室」词干的词；第二组是表示依恋的形容词，区别在于依据与温度。

entries.definition: The same Latin word borrowed directly and later: it asks what the law permits, while the adjective under study asks whom one will not abandon.
entries.definitionCN: 同一个拉丁词后来被直接借入：它问法律允许什么，而本词问的是不肯背弃谁。

entries.definition: The noun built on the same stem: it names the quality that a faithful person or act shows.
entries.definitionCN: 由同一词干构成的名词：它命名的是忠实的人或行为所显现的品质。

entries.definition: It looks close and even rhymes, but it comes from Latin regalis, from rex 'king', so it shares no root with this word.
entries.definitionCN: 它词形相近甚至押韵，但来自拉丁 regalis，源于 rex「国王」，与本词不同源。

entries.definition: Built on the same law noun with a verb for carrying: it names the making of statutes and has nothing to do with devotion.
entries.definitionCN: 同一法律名词加上表示「携带」的动词构成：它指制定法令，与忠贞无关。

entries.definition: Keeps promises and vows, especially in marriage or religion; this word adds the idea of belonging to a group or cause.
entries.definitionCN: 信守承诺与誓言，多用于婚姻或宗教；本词则多出「归属于某个团体或事业」之意。

entries.definition: Gives deep affection and time to a person or activity; it is warmer than the word under study and less about obligation.
entries.definitionCN: 对某人或某活动付出深厚感情与时间；它比本词更温暖，也更少涉及义务。

entries.definition: Holds a position without wavering, often through danger or criticism; it stresses firmness rather than attachment.
entries.definitionCN: 不动摇地守住立场，常在危险或批评之中；它强调坚定，而非依恋。

entries.definition: Stays the same across years and moods; it describes steadiness of behaviour, not the bond that produces it.
entries.definitionCN: 多年间、在各种情绪下都保持不变；它描述行为的一贯，而不描述产生这种一贯的纽带。

normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的「法律」词根及其双重借入词、由同一词干长出的真实同族词、真实固定搭配，以及把这个词义拉得最远的政治说法。

normal.en: The root is the Latin word for law, and the earliest sense was the lawful man, so the adjective began as a legal description.
normal.cn: 词根是拉丁语中表示「法律」的词，最早的意思就是守法之人，所以这个形容词起初是一种法律描述。

normal.en: The same Latin source entered English twice: once through Old French as this word, later directly as the adjective for what the law permits.
normal.cn: 同一个拉丁来源两次进入英语：一次经古法语成为本词，后来又一次直接成为表示「法律许可」的形容词。

normal.en: The family runs the noun for the quality, the adverb, the person noun, and both negative forms.
normal.cn: 同族词包括表示这种品质的名词、副词、表示效忠者的人物名词，以及两个否定形式。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the usual objects: a loyal friend, a loyal customer, a loyal supporter, and the frame loyal to someone.
normal.cn: 固定搭配显示它常接的对象：忠实的朋友、忠实的顾客、忠实的支持者，以及「忠于某人」的框架。

normal.en: The phrase loyal opposition shows that loyalty can survive open disagreement, because it is owed to the whole.
normal.cn: 「制度内忠诚的反对」这一说法表明，忠诚可以容纳公开分歧，因为它所向的是整体。

abstract.en: Picture a name carved inside a doorframe, where only the owner ever sees it.
abstract.cn: 想象门框内侧刻着一个名字，只有屋主自己看得见。

abstract.en: Picture a key that opens a shop nobody else bothers to open any more.
abstract.cn: 想象一把钥匙，打开一间别人都不再来开的店。

abstract.en: Picture a flag still flying over a post that the map has already forgotten.
abstract.cn: 想象一面旗仍飘在地图已经遗忘的哨所上。

examples.en: The village remained loyal to its old doctor and refused to replace him with a younger one.
examples.cn: 村民始终忠于那位老医生，不肯换一位更年轻的来替代他。

examples.en: A loyal customer is worth more than a clever advertisement.
examples.cn: 一位忠实的顾客，比一则聪明的广告更有价值。

examples.en: She was loyal to the promise she had made, though no one would ever have known.
examples.cn: 她信守自己许下的承诺，尽管这件事永远不会有人知道。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「老友」——把你当老朋友的人，风雨里也不会走开

root: 古法语 loial ← 拉丁 legalis「法律的」← lex「法律」；lex 更深来源不确定，与 legere「收集、读」的关联仅为假说；本词与表示「法律的」的那个英语形容词，是同一拉丁词的两次借入，即双重借入。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one movement: a bond is chosen and then repeatedly honoured, towards a person, a group, an oath, a shop, a principle, a partner, a state, and finally towards a whole that one may criticise.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着同一个动作展开：先选定一条纽带，然后一次次守住它——对人、对团体、对誓言、对一家店、对原则、对伴侣、对国家，最后是对一个可以批评的整体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a man still opening a shop whose founder is long dead and whose sign has faded.
core.cn: 核心意象：创办人早已去世、招牌已经褪色，那个人仍然每天来开门。

branches.en: TWO PEOPLE: friendship and romance are the same promise kept across time and distance.
branches.cn: 两个人：友情与爱情，是同一条跨过时间与距离而被守住的承诺。

branches.en: A BODY ONE BELONGS TO: a club, a party or a crown can claim the same sworn attachment.
branches.cn: 一个自己归属的集体：俱乐部、党派或王室，都能要求同一种宣誓般的归属。

branches.en: AN OBLIGATION: an oath and a principle both bind without anyone watching.
branches.cn: 一项义务：誓言与原则都在无人注视时依然约束人。

branches.en: REPEATED CHOICE: trade measures loyalty by the customer who still returns.
branches.cn: 重复的选择：商业用「顾客是否仍然回来」来衡量忠诚。

branches.en: LOYALTY THAT CRITICISES: belonging to the whole can survive disagreement with its government.
branches.cn: 会批评的忠诚：归属于整体，可以容纳与其政府之间的分歧。

intro.en: This adjective came from Old French, built on the Latin law noun; the whole family can be read through that noun and its endings.
intro.cn: 这个形容词来自古法语，建立在拉丁「法律」名词之上；整个词族都可以顺着这个名词及其词尾读出来。

latinIntro.en: Latin lex supplies the noun, legalis turns it into an adjective of belonging, and Old French reshaped that adjective before English borrowed it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 lex 提供名词，legalis 把它变成表示「属于」的形容词，古法语又对这个形容词做了改造，之后英语才借入。

items.example: The root names the law that the faithful man was first said to keep.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根点出那个守法之人最初所守的法律。

items.example: The adjective turned the noun into a description of a person.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词把名词变成了对人的描述。

items.example: Old French shifted the sense from lawful to faithful before English took the word.
items.exampleCN: 古法语把词义从「合法的」转为「忠实的」，之后英语才借入。

items.meaning: faithful to a person or cause
items.example: He stayed loyal to the little studio long after its founder had died.
items.exampleCN: 创办人去世很久之后，他仍忠于那间小照相馆。

items.example: The club rewarded forty years of loyalty with a single chair.
items.exampleCN: 俱乐部用一把椅子回报了四十年的忠诚。

items.example: He served loyally through three changes of owner.
items.exampleCN: 他忠实地服务，经历了三次换主。

items.meaning: one who stays faithful to a government or cause
items.example: The loyalists refused to leave the town when the government fell.
items.exampleCN: 政府倒台时，效忠者拒绝离开这座城。

items.example: A disloyal ally is more dangerous than an open enemy.
items.exampleCN: 不忠的盟友比公开的敌人更危险。

definition_zh: 忠诚；忠心；效忠；（对品牌、球队等的）忠实；专一
definition_en: the quality of being faithful to a person, group or cause, and of not abandoning it in hard times
core_image: 一枚旧徽章别在内侧衣襟上，从不示人，也从不取下
scene: 球队降级那年，看台上仍有一批人穿着旧球衣来，季票一张也没退。Their loyalty survived the season in which the club lost every home match.
sceneCN: 这里 loyalty 指「对某个群体的忠心，不因处境变坏而撤离」（第 1 个义项：对人与群体的忠诚）；句意为他们的忠诚熬过了球队主场全败的那个赛季。可辨识物件：旧球衣、季票、空荡的看台、记分牌；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 忠诚；忠心；效忠；忠实；专一

senses.title: Faithfulness to a person or group
senses.definition: steady faithfulness to the people one belongs with, kept even when leaving would be easier
senses.definitionCN: 对自己所属之人保持稳定的忠心，即使离开更容易也不离开
senses.example: Their loyalty survived the season in which the club lost every home match.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的忠诚熬过了球队主场全败的那个赛季。
senses.why: The word began in feudal law as the faithfulness a sworn man owed his lord, so its heart is staying when one could go.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初是封建法律中宣誓者对领主的忠贞，核心就是「本可以走却留下」。

senses.title: Allegiance to a state or crown
senses.definition: the formal allegiance a citizen or subject owes to a state, flag or monarch
senses.definitionCN: 公民或臣民对国家、旗帜或君主承担的正式效忠
senses.example: New citizens swear loyalty to the constitution, not to a person.
senses.exampleCN: 新公民宣誓效忠的是宪法，而不是某个人。
senses.why: Feudal faithfulness was taken over by the modern state and attached to an institution rather than a lord.
senses.whyCN: 封建的忠贞被现代国家接手，系在制度上而不是系在领主身上。

senses.title: Sticking with an organisation or team
senses.titleCN: 对组织、球队的忠实追随
senses.definition: the attachment of a member or supporter who keeps supporting a body through poor results
senses.definitionCN: 成员或支持者的归属感：即使成绩不佳也继续支持某个团体
senses.example: Season-ticket holders showed a loyalty that no relegation could shake.
senses.exampleCN: 季票持有者表现出一种降级也摇不动的忠诚。
senses.why: Modern membership moved the old sworn bond into clubs, schools and companies, where nobody has sworn anything.
senses.whyCN: 现代的成员身份把古老的宣誓纽带移进俱乐部、学校与公司，而在那里并没有人宣过誓。

senses.title: Fidelity to an idea
senses.definition: attachment to a principle or cause that survives changes in fashion and cost
senses.definitionCN: 对某项原则或事业的坚持，不因风气与代价的改变而放弃
senses.example: Her loyalty to the reform outlasted three leaders who had promised it.
senses.exampleCN: 她对改革的支持比三位承诺改革的人任期都长。
senses.why: Once the object of faithfulness is no longer a person, loyalty becomes consistency of principle.
senses.whyCN: 当忠贞的对象不再是某个人，忠诚就变成原则上的前后一致。

senses.title: Repeated buying from one brand
senses.titleCN: 对某一品牌的消费忠实
senses.definition: in business, a customer's habit of returning to the same brand or shop instead of switching
senses.definitionCN: 商业中指顾客习惯性回到同一品牌或店铺而不转投他家
senses.example: The airline measured loyalty by how often passengers chose it over a cheaper rival.
senses.exampleCN: 这家航空公司用乘客在多选更便宜的对手时仍选它的频率来衡量忠诚度。
senses.why: Marketing borrowed a moral word for a statistical habit, which is why loyalty programmes can be bought.
senses.whyCN: 营销借用一个道德词来描述统计习惯，所以「忠诚计划」是可以买的。

senses.title: Faithfulness in a close relationship
senses.definition: the promise of exclusivity and steadiness between partners
senses.definitionCN: 伴侣之间专一而稳定的承诺
senses.example: He treated loyalty as a daily practice rather than a single promise.
senses.exampleCN: 他把专一当成每天要做的事，而不是一次性的承诺。
senses.why: The oldest personal sense narrows here to the intimacy of a couple, where faithfulness is tested privately.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的对人之义在这里收窄到伴侣的亲密关系，忠贞在私下受到检验。

senses.title: Doing one's duty faithfully
senses.definition: the reliable performance of a role, especially when nobody is watching or rewarding it
senses.definitionCN: 可靠地履行职责，尤其在无人监督或奖赏时
senses.example: The night guard's loyalty was never noticed until the flood came.
senses.exampleCN: 直到洪水来临，人们才注意到夜班守卫的忠于职守。
senses.why: From faithfulness to persons, the word extends to faithfulness to a task and to those the task protects.
senses.whyCN: 从对人的忠贞，这个词延伸到对任务的忠实，以及对任务所护之人的忠实。

senses.title: Competing allegiances
senses.titleCN: 多重而相互冲突的效忠
senses.definition: in the plural, the several claims on a person's faithfulness that may pull in different directions
senses.definitionCN: 复数形式指一个人所背负的多种效忠要求，它们可能指向不同方向
senses.example: Divided loyalties made the minister's decision impossible to defend.
senses.exampleCN: 两头为难的效忠让这位部长的决定无法自辩。
senses.why: A person can belong to a family, a firm and a country at once, and the plural names the conflict rather than the virtue.
senses.whyCN: 一个人同时属于家庭、公司与国家，复数形式指的是这种冲突，而不是美德本身。

intro.en: Loyalty comes from Old French loialté, from Latin legalis 'of the law', from lex 'law'. English legal is the same Latin word borrowed later and directly, so loyal and legal are doublets.
intro.cn: loyalty 来自古法语 loialté，源头是拉丁 legalis「法律的」，再上溯为 lex「法律」。英语的 legal 是同一个拉丁词后来直接借入的形式，因此 loyal 与 legal 是同一词根的两次借入。

items.en: Lex meant law or statute. Its origin is uncertain; a link with the verb legere 'to gather, read' is generally mentioned but not proven, so it is a hypothesis rather than a settled derivation.
items.cn: lex 意为法律、法令。其来源不确定；常有人把它与动词 legere「收集、读」联系起来，但这只是假说，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: Legalis meant 'belonging to the law'. In medieval usage it also described someone who keeps the law, and so someone who is faithful to an oath.
items.cn: legalis 意为「属于法律的」。在中世纪用法中，它也形容守法的人，进而形容忠于誓言的人。

items.en: Old French turned legalis into loial, where the sense had already shifted from lawful to faithful, especially faithful to a lord.
items.cn: 古法语把 legalis 变成 loial，词义已从「合法的」转为「忠实的」，尤其指对领主忠实。

items.en: The abstract noun loialte named that faithfulness, and English took it in the fourteenth century for the bond between a sworn man and his lord.
items.cn: 抽象名词 loialte 指这种忠贞，英语在十四世纪借入，用于宣誓者与领主之间的纽带。

items.en: English later borrowed legalis again, directly and unchanged in meaning, producing legal. Loyal and legal therefore look different and mean different things while sharing one Latin source.
items.cn: 英语后来又直接借入 legalis，词义未变，产生了 legal。因此 loyal 与 legal 形貌与含义都不同，却共享同一个拉丁来源。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the root of lex has no agreed explanation; the connection with the verb for gathering or reading is a common suggestion, not an established fact, and any Indo-European form offered for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：lex 的词根没有公认解释；与表示「收集、读」的动词之间的关联只是一种常见推测，并非既定事实，凡为其给出的印欧形式均属重构。

note.en: Group one holds words that share the Latin law root but arrived by a different route; group two holds near synonyms that differ in what the faithfulness is owed to.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁「法律」词根、但走了另一条路径的词；第二组是近义说法，区别在于忠诚所指向的对象。

entries.definition: The adjective built on the same stem; loyalty is the quality, loyal the description of a person or act that has it.
entries.definitionCN: 由同一词干构成的形容词；loyalty 是这种品质，loyal 则形容具备它的人或行为。

entries.definition: The same Latin source borrowed later and directly: it concerns what the law permits, not what faithfulness requires.
entries.definitionCN: 同一拉丁来源后来被直接借入：它关乎法律允许什么，而不关乎忠贞要求什么。

entries.definition: Built on the same law noun with a verb for carrying: it names the making of statutes and has nothing to do with devotion.
entries.definitionCN: 同一法律名词加上表示「携带」的动词构成：它指制定法令，与忠贞无关。

entries.definition: The person noun built on loyal; it usually names someone who stays with a government or cause when others leave.
entries.definitionCN: 由 loyal 构成的人物名词；通常指在别人离开时仍留在某政府或事业一边的人。

entries.definition: The keeping of promises and vows, often in marriage or religion; loyalty adds the idea of belonging to a group.
entries.definitionCN: 信守承诺与誓言，多用于婚姻或宗教；loyalty 更强调归属于某个群体。

entries.definition: Formal obligation of loyalty to a state or sovereign; it is public and sworn, while loyalty can be private and unspoken.
entries.definitionCN: 对国家或君主的正式效忠义务；它是公开的、宣誓的，而 loyalty 可以是私下且不言明的。

entries.definition: Faithfulness in a relationship, or exactness in copying; it stresses precision as much as devotion.
entries.definitionCN: 关系中的忠贞，或复制时的精确；它既强调 devotion，也强调准确。

entries.definition: Deep affection and dedication to a person or activity; it is warmer than loyalty and less concerned with obligation.
entries.definitionCN: 对某人或某活动的深厚感情与投入；它比 loyalty 更温暖，也更不涉及义务。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real law root, the real doublet legal, the real commercial phrases and the real adjective family.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的「法律」词根、真实的双借词 legal、真实的商业说法，以及真实的形容词词族。

normal.en: The root is the Latin word for law, so loyalty began as the faithfulness a sworn man owed under law.
normal.cn: 词根是拉丁语中表示「法律」的词，所以忠诚最初是宣誓者在法律之下所欠的忠贞。

normal.en: Legal is the same source borrowed a second time, which is why one word is about faithfulness and the other about permission.
normal.cn: legal 是同一来源的第二次借入，因此一个词关乎忠贞，另一个关乎许可。

normal.en: Business phrases mark the modern sense: brand loyalty, customer loyalty, a loyalty programme.
normal.cn: 商业说法标出现代义：品牌忠诚度、客户忠诚度、会员忠诚计划。

normal.en: The family runs loyalty, loyal, loyally, loyalist, disloyal and disloyalty.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 loyalty、loyal、loyally、loyalist、disloyal 与 disloyalty。

normal.en: The plural loyalties names conflicting claims, as in divided loyalties, rather than more of the same virtue.
normal.cn: 复数形式指的是相互冲突的多重效忠，也就是「两头为难」，而不是同一种美德变得更多。

abstract.en: Picture a badge worn inside the lapel where nobody can see it.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚徽章别在内侧衣襟上，谁也看不见。

abstract.en: Picture a seat kept empty for years in case someone returns.
abstract.cn: 想象一个空了许多年的座位，只为等某个人回来。

abstract.en: Picture a road walked in the same direction after every other walker has turned back.
abstract.cn: 想象在其他人都折返之后，仍朝同一方向走下去的一条路。

examples.en: The company rewards loyalty with early access rather than cash.
examples.cn: 公司用优先购买权而不是现金来回报忠诚。

examples.en: His loyalty to the department outlasted four directors.
examples.cn: 他对这个部门的忠诚比四任主管都长久。

examples.en: Divided loyalties kept her from speaking at the hearing.
examples.cn: 两头为难的效忠让她在听证会上无法开口。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「法律之下的守约」——受人以托、守约不弃，就是忠诚

root: 古法语 loialté ← 拉丁 legalis「法律的」← lex「法律」。英语 legal 是同一拉丁词后来的直接借入，故 loyal 与 legal 同源而异貌。lex 的更深词源不确定，与「收集、读」的关联仅为假说。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses begin with a sworn faithfulness to a person, then widen to a state, a team, an idea, a brand, a partner, a duty, and finally to the conflicts that arise when several of these claims meet in one life.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从对某个人的宣誓忠贞开始，再依次扩展到国家、团队、理念、品牌、伴侣、职责，最后落在多重效忠同时压到一个人身上时的冲突。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a badge worn on the inside of a lapel, never shown and never removed.
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚别在内侧衣襟上的徽章，从不示人，也从不取下。

branches.en: PERSONAL BOND: from a sworn man to a partner, faithfulness is tested in private.
branches.cn: 个人纽带：从宣誓者到伴侣，忠贞都在私下受到检验。

branches.en: THE STATE: the old bond is transferred to a constitution or a crown.
branches.cn: 国家：古老的纽带被移交给宪法或王冠。

branches.en: BELONGING AND BUYING: clubs and brands inherit the language of allegiance.
branches.cn: 归属与购买：俱乐部与品牌继承了效忠的语言。

branches.en: CAUSE AND DUTY: when no person is involved, loyalty becomes consistency and reliability.
branches.cn: 事业与职责：当对象不是人，忠诚就变成前后一致与可靠。

branches.en: THE SPLIT: the plural turns the virtue into a dilemma.
branches.cn: 分裂：复数形式把这份美德变成两难。

intro.en: Loyalty is a French abstract noun on a Latin law root, with a suffix that turns an adjective into a quality.
intro.cn: loyalty 是一个建在拉丁「法律」词根上的法语抽象名词，其词尾把形容词变成一种品质。

latinIntro.en: Latin lex supplies the stem, legalis supplies the adjective, and the French ending marks the abstract quality; the same stem also built legal and legislation.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 lex 提供词干，legalis 提供形容词，法语的词尾标出抽象品质；同一词干还造出了 legal 与 legislation。

items.example: The root names the law under which an oath is sworn.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根指誓言所依凭的法律。

items.example: The adjective shifted from lawful to faithful.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词从「合法的」转为「忠实的」。

items.example: A loial man kept his oath to his lord.
items.exampleCN: 忠实的人会守住对领主的誓言。

items.example: Their loyalty survived the season in which the club lost every home match.
items.exampleCN: 他们的忠诚熬过了球队主场全败的那个赛季。

items.example: A loyal reader renews before the deadline.
items.exampleCN: 忠实的读者会在截止前续订。

items.example: He served loyally for thirty years.
items.exampleCN: 他忠诚地服务了三十年。

items.example: The loyalists refused to leave the building.
items.exampleCN: 效忠者拒绝离开那栋楼。

items.example: The court treated silence as disloyalty.
items.exampleCN: 法庭把沉默当作不忠。

definition_zh: 运气；好运；侥幸；时运
definition_en: the force that seems to decide events by chance; also good fortune and success that comes without skill
core_image: 一枚硬币在空中翻转，落下时正好卡在指尖上方，摇摇欲坠却没有倒
scene: 码头边，渔夫把最后一网兜拉上来，网里空空的，可转身时却在木板上看见一枚别人掉下的硬币。Luck came to him at the very moment he had stopped expecting anything.
sceneCN: 这里 luck 是「好运、幸运」（第 2 个义项：带来好结果的好运）；句意为运气在他不再期待的时候降临。画面里可认出码头、空网兜与木板上的硬币。

derivatives.zh: 由 luck 加形容词后缀 -y 构成，义为「幸运的」
由 lucky 变 y 为 i 再加 -ly 构成，义为「幸运地；幸好」
由 luck 加表示「没有」的后缀 -less 构成，义为「运气不好的」

senses.title: Chance seen as a force that shapes events
senses.definition: the force that seems to decide events by chance, whether the outcome is good or bad
senses.definitionCN: 似乎在冥冥中决定事情成败的偶然力量，无论结果是好是坏
senses.example: No one can explain why the storm missed the village; they put it down to luck.
senses.exampleCN: 谁也说不清风暴为什么绕过了村子，他们把它归因于运气。
senses.why: When people cannot explain why a plan succeeds or fails, they name the unknown cause luck, so the word first stands in for chance itself.
senses.whyCN: 当人们说不清一个计划为何成功或失败时，就把这个未知的原因叫作 luck，所以这个词最初是「偶然本身」的代称。

senses.title: Good fortune that brings favourable results
senses.definition: good fortune, especially when it brings success, safety or an advantage
senses.definitionCN: 尤指带来成功、平安或优势的好运气
senses.example: It was pure luck that the last seat went to her.
senses.exampleCN: 最后那个座位落到她手里，纯属好运。
senses.why: Because people most often speak of luck when things turn out well, the neutral force narrowed into the favourable sense that dominates everyday use.
senses.whyCN: 因为人们通常在事情顺利时才提起 luck，这个中性的力量就收窄成日常最常用的「好运气」义。

senses.title: Success that comes by chance rather than skill
senses.definition: a favourable result that happened by accident rather than through skill or planning
senses.definitionCN: 凭偶然而非技巧或计划取得的有利结果
senses.example: The team won by luck rather than by better play.
senses.exampleCN: 这支队伍是靠侥幸而不是靠更好的发挥赢的。
senses.why: If good fortune can deliver a result, then a result delivered that way is itself called luck, so the cause and the outcome share one word.
senses.whyCN: 如果好运能带来结果，那么以这种方式得到的结果本身也被叫作 luck，于是原因与结果共用同一个词。

senses.title: One's personal fortune at a particular time
senses.definition: the state of a person's fortune at a given moment, which can rise or fall
senses.definitionCN: 一个人在某一时刻的运气状态，可升可降
senses.example: His luck changed the moment the manager noticed his work.
senses.exampleCN: 经理注意到他的工作那一刻，他的运势就变了。
senses.why: Luck as a force can also be treated as something a person possesses, so English speaks of someone's luck rising, falling or running out.
senses.whyCN: 作为力量的 luck 也可以被看成一个人所拥有的东西，于是英语会说某人的运气上升、下降或用完。

intro.en: Luck enters English in the fifteenth century from a Germanic source; its exact path is uncertain, but gambling gave it a firm place in everyday speech.
intro.cn: luck 于十五世纪从日耳曼语来源进入英语；确切路径不确定，但赌博让它在日常语言中站稳了脚。

items.en: Luck appears in written English in the fifteenth century as lucke, meaning good fortune.
items.cn: luck 在十五世纪以 lucke 的形式出现在书面英语中，意为好运。

items.en: Most accounts link it to Middle Dutch luc or the related Low German gelucke, though the exact path is not certain.
items.cn: 多数说法把它与中古荷兰语 luc 或相关的低地德语 gelucke 联系起来，但确切来源路径并不确定。

items.en: In the sixteenth century the word was common at dice and card tables, where fortune was visibly decided by chance.
items.cn: 十六世纪时这个词常用于骰子和牌桌，在那里运气明显由偶然决定。

items.en: From games it widened to any event that people believed chance had decided.
items.cn: 它从游戏扩展到人们认为由偶然决定的任何事情。

items.en: Modern English uses luck for chance as a force, for good fortune, and for success that came without skill.
items.cn: 现代英语用 luck 指作为力量的偶然、好运气，以及不靠技巧而得来的成功。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the luck family and a spelling neighbour; the near-meaning group collects words for chance and for what fortune brings.
note.cn: 形近组收 luck 词族与一个拼写相近的词；近义组收表示偶然以及命运所带来之物的词。

entries.definition: Having good fortune; built from luck with -y.
entries.definitionCN: 有好运的；由 luck 加 -y 构成。

entries.definition: By good fortune; fortunately.
entries.definitionCN: 幸运地；幸好。

entries.definition: Without good fortune, and often unfortunate.
entries.definitionCN: 运气不好的，常指倒霉。

entries.definitionCN: 挂在链上的小盒；只是拼写与 luck 相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: Chance or the good and bad things it brings.
entries.definitionCN: 偶然，以及它带来的好坏遭遇。

entries.definition: The possibility that something will happen, or events without a plan.
entries.definitionCN: 某事发生的可能性，或没有计划的事件。

entries.definition: The power believed to fix what will happen to a person.
entries.definitionCN: 被认为决定一个人遭遇的力量；命运。

entries.definition: A person's future seen as already settled.
entries.definitionCN: 被视为早已定下的人生归宿。

entries.definition: Bad luck or an unlucky event.
entries.definitionCN: 坏运气或不幸的事件。

normalIntro.en: The word is short and its origin uncertain, so the hooks come from its family, its fixed phrases and its long association with games of chance.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词很短，来源又不确定，所以记忆钩子来自它的词族、固定短语，以及它与碰运气游戏的长期联系。

normal.en: Lucky is luck plus -y, so the adjective simply means full of luck.
normal.cn: lucky 是 luck 加 -y，所以这个形容词的意思就是「带着运气的」。

normal.en: Luckily changes the y of lucky to i before adding -ly.
normal.cn: luckily 是先把 lucky 的 y 变成 i，再加 -ly。

normal.en: Luckless adds -less, the suffix of absence, so it means without luck.
normal.cn: luckless 加的是表示「没有」的后缀 -less，因此意为没有运气。

normal.en: By luck is a fixed phrase for something that happened through chance rather than plan.
normal.cn: by luck 是固定短语，指事情靠偶然而非计划发生。

normal.en: Luck out is informal and means to succeed by chance, keeping the old gambling flavour.
normal.cn: luck out 是口语说法，意为碰巧成功，保留了旧日赌博的意味。

abstract.en: A word for an unexplained cause becomes a word for a personal possession, because people would rather own fortune than admit they cannot explain it.
abstract.cn: 一个指无法解释之原因的词，变成了指个人所有物的词，因为人宁愿把运气归为己有，也不愿承认自己解释不了。

abstract.en: Luck sits between chance and fate: less planned than fate, more personal than pure chance.
abstract.cn: luck 处在偶然与命运之间：比命运更少安排，比纯粹的偶然更带个人色彩。

abstract.en: Every wish of good luck admits the same thing: the outcome is not fully in our hands.
abstract.cn: 每一句祝好运都承认同一件事：结果并不完全掌握在我们手里。

examples.en: It was pure luck that the last seat went to her.
examples.cn: 最后那个座位落到她手里，纯属好运。

examples.en: The team won by luck rather than by better play.
examples.cn: 这支队伍是靠侥幸而不是靠更好的发挥赢的。

examples.en: His luck changed the moment the manager noticed his work.
examples.cn: 经理注意到他的工作那一刻，他的运势就变了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「拉壳」——抽奖时一拉就开出好壳，记住 luck 是运气。

root: 来源不确定；一般认为与中古荷兰语 luc 或低地德语 gelucke 有关，十五世纪进入英语时意为好运；没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is chance as an unnamed force; the senses narrow into good fortune, then into success by accident and a person's shifting fortune.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是把偶然看作一种无名的力量；义项收窄为好运气，再分为意外得来的成功与个人起伏的运势。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a coin spinning in the air and landing upright on a fingertip, trembling but not falling.
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚硬币在空中翻转，落下时立在上方不稳，却始终没有倒下。

branches.en: a storm that turns aside for no clear reason
branches.cn: 毫无缘由地转向的风暴

branches.en: the last ticket going to the person who arrived late
branches.cn: 最后一张票落到迟到者手里

branches.en: a coin landing the right way at a card table
branches.cn: 牌桌上硬币恰好落在对的一面

branches.en: a weak side winning without doing anything clever
branches.cn: 弱队没使出什么高招却赢了

branches.en: a worker noticed just as his fortunes turn
branches.cn: 正逢运势转折时被注意到的工人

intro.en: Luck is a short Germanic noun, and English builds its family with two suffixes that mark presence and absence of fortune.
intro.cn: luck 是一个简短的日耳曼语名词，英语用两个后缀分别表示「有运气」与「没有运气」，撑起整个词族。

latinIntro.en: Luck comes from a Germanic source of uncertain path, so no reliable Latin cognate is recorded for it.
latinIntro.cn: luck 来自路径不确定的日耳曼语来源，因此没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.exampleCN: 运气在救援中起了作用。

items.exampleCN: 幸好比赛前雨停了。

definition_zh: 幸运的；走运的；带来好运的；吉利的；侥幸的
definition_en: having good fortune; bringing good fortune; happening by chance in a favourable way; or believed to be auspicious
core_image: 一个人从口袋里摸出一张旧彩票，对着光一看，号码正好全部对上
scene: 雨刚停，一个赶路的人随手招了一下，空荡荡的街口竟真的停下一辆出租车。He felt lucky as the taxi pulled up beside him.
sceneCN: 这里 lucky 是「幸运的、走运的」（第 1 个义项：本人有好运）；句意为出租车在他身边停下时，他感到自己很走运。画面里可认出雨后的街口与停下的出租车。

pos.zh: 幸运的；走运的；带来好运的；吉利的；侥幸的

collocations.zh: 难得的好机会；意外的好运

由 lucky 加否定前缀 un- 构成，义为「不幸的；不吉利的」

senses.title: Having good fortune in a particular situation
senses.definition: enjoying good fortune, especially when something good happens by chance
senses.definitionCN: 享有好运，尤指好事偶然落到自己头上
senses.example: She felt lucky when the last ticket was still available.
senses.exampleCN: 最后一张票还没卖掉，她觉得自己很幸运。
senses.why: The noun luck names the force, and the suffix -y turns it into a quality, so a person can be described as having that force on their side.
senses.whyCN: 名词 luck 指这种力量，后缀 -y 把它变成一种性质，于是可以说一个人身上带着这种力量。

senses.title: Believed to bring good fortune to its owner
senses.definition: thought to bring good fortune to the person who has it or carries it
senses.definitionCN: 被认为能给拥有者或携带者带来好运的
senses.example: He wore the same shirt to every match because he believed it was lucky.
senses.exampleCN: 每逢比赛他都穿同一件衬衫，因为他相信那件衣服能带来好运。
senses.why: If a person can be lucky, then an object can be trusted to carry that luck, so the word spreads from people to charms and clothes.
senses.whyCN: 既然人可以走运，人们也会相信某件物品能承载这份运气，于是词义从人扩展到护身符和衣物。

senses.title: Happening by chance in a favourable way
senses.definition: favourable but produced by accident rather than by skill or knowledge
senses.definitionCN: 结果有利，却出自偶然而非技巧或知识
senses.example: It was a lucky guess, not real knowledge.
senses.exampleCN: 那只是侥幸猜中，并不是真懂。
senses.why: When a good result arrives without skill, English calls it lucky, because the outcome is credited to fortune rather than to the person.
senses.whyCN: 当好结果并非来自技巧时，英语称其为 lucky，因为这个结果被归功于运气而不是归功于人。

senses.title: Considered auspicious for a particular purpose
senses.definition: believed to be a favourable time, number or sign for something
senses.definitionCN: 被认为对某件事有利的时间、数字或征兆
senses.example: They chose the date because it was a lucky day in the old calendar.
senses.exampleCN: 他们选这个日期，是因为它在旧历里是幸运日。
senses.why: From charms the word extends to days, numbers and signs, because people look for fortune not only in objects but also in timing.
senses.whyCN: 从护身符出发，这个词又扩展到日子、数字与征兆，因为人们不只在物件里找运气，也在时机里找。

intro.en: Lucky is the noun luck with the adjective suffix -y; the noun itself came into English from a Germanic source whose exact path is uncertain.
intro.cn: lucky 是名词 luck 加形容词后缀 -y；这个名词本身来自日耳曼语来源，确切路径不确定。

items.en: Luck enters English in the fifteenth century, and the adjective lucky follows by adding -y to the noun.
items.cn: luck 于十五世纪进入英语，形容词 lucky 由名词加 -y 随后产生。

items.en: The noun is generally linked to Middle Dutch luc or Low German gelucke, though the exact source remains uncertain.
items.cn: 这个名词一般认为与中古荷兰语 luc 或低地德语 gelucke 有关，确切来源仍不确定。

items.en: Lucky appears in the sixteenth century, first around games of chance and then in ordinary speech.
items.cn: lucky 在十六世纪出现，最初用于碰运气的游戏，后来进入日常语言。

items.en: The suffix -y turns nouns into adjectives, as it does in health to healthy and luck to lucky.
items.cn: 后缀 -y 把名词变成形容词，health 变 healthy、luck 变 lucky 都是这样。

items.en: Modern English uses lucky for people, charms, guesses, breaks and auspicious days.
items.cn: 现代英语用 lucky 形容人、护身符、猜测、好机会与吉日。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the luck family and a word that merely rhymes; the near-meaning group collects adjectives for good fortune and its opposite.
note.cn: 形近组收 luck 词族与一个只是押韵的词；近义组收表示好运及其反面的形容词。

entries.definition: The noun behind lucky, meaning chance or good fortune.
entries.definitionCN: lucky 背后的名词，意为运气或好运。

entries.definition: By good fortune; the adverb built from lucky.
entries.definitionCN: 幸运地；由 lucky 构成的副词。

entries.definition: Having bad fortune; lucky with the negative prefix un-.
entries.definitionCN: 运气不好的；lucky 加否定前缀 un-。

entries.definition: Brave in a difficult situation; only the ending is close, and the root is different.
entries.definitionCN: 在困境中勇敢的；只是词尾与 lucky 相近，词根不同。

entries.definition: Having good fortune, often in a formal tone.
entries.definitionCN: 有好运的，语气常较正式。

entries.definition: Enjoying good fortune that is seen as a gift.
entries.definitionCN: 享有被视为恩赐的好运。

entries.definition: Given special help, advantage or preference.
entries.definitionCN: 得到特别帮助、优势或偏爱的。

entries.definition: Protected as if by magic; often a light or ironic word.
entries.definitionCN: 像受魔法保护般的；常带轻松或反讽语气。

entries.definition: Marked by bad fortune from the start.
entries.definitionCN: 从一开始就注定倒霉的。

normalIntro.en: The word is a transparent suffix build from luck, so its hooks come from the noun, the -y suffix and the spelling changes in comparison.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词由 luck 加后缀清楚构成，记忆钩子来自名词、-y 后缀以及比较级中的拼写变化。

normal.en: Lucky is luck plus -y, so the adjective means having or carrying luck.
normal.cn: lucky 是 luck 加 -y，所以这个形容词意为拥有或带着运气。

normal.en: The comparative is luckier: the final y becomes i before -er is added.
normal.cn: 比较级是 luckier：最后的 y 先变成 i，再加 -er。

normal.en: The superlative is luckiest, following the same y to i change.
normal.cn: 最高级是 luckiest，同样先把 y 变成 i。

normal.en: Unlucky adds the prefix un- to lucky and reverses the fortune.
normal.cn: unlucky 在 lucky 前加前缀 un-，把运气反过来。

normal.en: Lucky break and lucky charm are fixed phrases, one for a chance opportunity and one for a trusted object.
normal.cn: lucky break 与 lucky charm 是固定短语，一个指偶然得来的机会，一个指被信赖的物件。

abstract.en: Calling a shirt lucky shows how easily people move fortune out of the body and into an object they can control.
abstract.cn: 把一件衬衫说成幸运，说明人很容易把运气从身体转移到一件自己能控制的物品上。

abstract.en: A lucky guess is praised and distrusted at once, because we want the result but not the randomness behind it.
abstract.cn: 侥幸猜中同时得到赞许与怀疑，因为我们想要结果，却不喜欢结果背后的偶然。

abstract.en: A lucky day is a way of making time itself take sides with a plan.
abstract.cn: 吉日是一种让时间本身站在计划一边的说法。

examples.en: She felt lucky when the last ticket was still available.
examples.cn: 最后一张票还没卖掉，她觉得自己很幸运。

examples.en: He wore the same shirt to every match because he believed it was lucky.
examples.cn: 每逢比赛他都穿同一件衬衫，因为他相信那件衣服能带来好运。

examples.en: It was a lucky guess, not real knowledge.
examples.cn: 那只是侥幸猜中，并不是真懂。

branches.cn: 放在外套口袋里的护身符

definition_zh: 行李；旅行箱包；辎重
definition_en: the bags, cases and other containers that a traveller carries, spoken of as a group without a plural, or in older use the baggage that moved with an army

scene: 出发前一晚，客厅地板上堆着几只箱子和旅行袋，拉链还敞着。She packed her luggage the night before the flight and left it by the door.

senses.title: Bags and cases carried on a journey
senses.definition: the bags, suitcases and other containers in which a traveller carries personal things
senses.definitionCN: 旅行者用来装个人物品的箱包等容器的总称
senses.example: She packed her luggage the night before the flight.
senses.exampleCN: 出发前一晚，她收拾好了行李。
senses.why: The word began as the mass of things lugged along on a journey, so it names the load as a whole rather than each separate bag; English keeps it uncountable because the group, not the item, is what the word points at.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指旅途中被拖着走的那一堆东西，命名的是整批负担而不是某一只包；英语让它保持不可数，因为词所指向的是这一整堆，而不是其中的单件。

senses.title: An item counted by the piece
senses.definition: a traveller's bags when they are counted or weighed one piece at a time, as at an airport desk
senses.definitionCN: 在机场柜台等场合按件数或重量逐件清点的旅行箱包
senses.example: How many pieces of luggage are you checking in?
senses.exampleCN: 你要托运几件行李？
senses.why: Because the noun has no plural of its own, English counts the load through a phrase such as a piece of; the piece becomes the unit while the word itself stays collective.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个名词本身没有复数形式，英语便借「一件」这样的说法来计数；于是「件」成了单位，而这个词本身仍保持集体含义。

senses.title: The baggage of an army
senses.definition: in older use, the carts, supplies and bags that moved with an army on the march
senses.definitionCN: 旧时指随军队行进的车马、补给与包袋
senses.example: The column halted while its luggage was brought up.
senses.exampleCN: 队伍停下来，等辎重跟上来。
senses.why: An army on the march drags the same kind of load as a traveller, so the word was widened from personal bags to the whole train of supplies that follows the soldiers.
senses.whyCN: 行军中的军队拖着与旅人同类的一堆东西，于是这个词从个人箱包扩展到跟随士兵的整套补给车队。

intro.en: Luggage is an English noun usually explained as the verb lug plus the suffix -age, and it has meant both a traveller's bags and an army's baggage.
intro.cn: luggage 是一个英语名词，一般解释为动词 lug 加后缀 -age 构成；它既指旅行者的箱包，也指军队的辎重。

items.en: The earliest luggage names the mass of bags and gear dragged along on a journey, and the same word could also mean a bundle tied up for carrying.
items.cn: 最早的 luggage 指旅途中被拖着走的那一堆包袋与器具，同一个词也可指捆好待扛的一束东西。

items.en: It is generally explained as the verb lug, to drag or carry with effort, plus the noun suffix -age; the deeper origin of lug itself is uncertain, so the chain is plausible rather than proved.
items.cn: 一般认为它由动词 lug（吃力地拖、扛）加名词后缀 -age 构成；但 lug 本身更早的来源并不确定，所以这条构词链只能算合理推断，而非定论。

items.en: By the sixteenth century luggage settles on the bags of a traveller, while the older military sense survives for the baggage train of an army.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，luggage 稳定指旅行者的箱包，而更早的军事义仍保留下来，用来指军队的辎重队。

items.en: Steamers and railways made luggage a fixed term for personal bags, and British usage kept it while American usage preferred baggage.
items.cn: 轮船与铁路使 luggage 成为指个人行李的固定说法，英式沿用这个词，美式则更常用 baggage。

items.en: Modern English keeps luggage uncountable, counts it in pieces, and builds compounds such as hand luggage and luggage allowance.
items.cn: 现代英语让 luggage 保持不可数，用「件」来计数，并构成 hand luggage、luggage allowance 之类的复合词。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the root verb and the compounds built on luggage; the near-meaning group gathers other words for bags and travel loads.
note.cn: 形近组收它的词根动词以及由 luggage 构成的复合词；近义组收其他表示箱包与旅途负载的词。

normalIntro.en: The word is built on a verb for dragging, and its family keeps returning to loads that are hauled rather than neatly carried.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在表示「拖拽」的动词上，同族词反复回到被拖着走、而非轻巧提着的负载。

normal.en: Luggage rests on the verb lug, to drag something heavy, so the word pictures bags being hauled along a platform.
normal.cn: luggage 建立在动词 lug（吃力地拖）之上，所以这个词画出的画面是在站台上拖着一堆包走。

normal.en: The suffix -age turns a verb into a mass noun, which is why luggage has no plural and behaves like baggage.
normal.cn: 后缀 -age 把动词变成集体名词，所以 luggage 没有复数，用法与 baggage 相同。

normal.en: British travellers say luggage where Americans often say baggage, and neither word takes an s.
normal.cn: 英国旅客说 luggage，美国人常说 baggage，两个词都不加 s。

normal.en: Hand luggage stays with the passenger while check-in luggage goes into the hold, so the compounds sort the load by where it travels.
normal.cn: hand luggage 随乘客走，check-in luggage 进舱底，这些复合词按行李的去处分门别类。

normal.en: A luggage tag carries your name because a bag pulled off a belt belongs to nobody until it is marked.
normal.cn: 行李牌上写着名字，因为从传送带上取下的包在没有标记之前不属于任何人。

abstract.en: A word for dragged bags suggests that travel is measured less by distance than by what you insist on carrying.
abstract.cn: 一个表示「拖行李」的词暗示，衡量旅程的不是距离，而是你坚持要带走的东西。

abstract.en: Luggage has no plural because a traveller's load is felt as one weight rather than as separate objects.
abstract.cn: luggage 没有复数，因为旅人的负载被感受为一整个重量，而不是分开的物件。

abstract.en: Every bag has a tag, and every tag is a small claim that says this weight is mine.
abstract.cn: 每只包都有牌子，每块牌子都是一个微小的声明：这份重量属于我。

definition_zh: 块；团；肿块；把……归并；勉强接受
definition_en: a solid mass with no regular shape, a swelling on the body, to group separate things into one mass, or to accept something unpleasant because there is no other choice

scene: 厨房台面上放着一袋刚买回来的方糖，其中几块粘成了不规则的一团。He dropped a lump of sugar into the hot tea and watched it sink.
sceneCN: 这里 lump 是「块、团」（第 1 个义项：无定形的固体块）；句意为他往热茶里丢了一块方糖，看着它沉下去。图中可辨识物件：厨房台面、方糖袋、茶杯。

senses.title: A solid mass with no regular shape
senses.definition: a piece of solid material that has no regular shape and is felt as one heavy mass
senses.definitionCN: 一块没有规则形状、被感知为一整个沉重整体的固体
senses.example: He dropped a lump of sugar into the hot tea.
senses.exampleCN: 他往热茶里丢了一块方糖。
senses.why: The word starts from what the hand feels: a portion of material that has set or been pressed into one body, with no edges worth counting.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从手的触感出发：一部分材料凝成或压成了一整块，边上没有值得去数的棱角。

senses.title: A swelling under the skin
senses.definition: an area of the body that has risen into a hard or rounded swelling
senses.definitionCN: 身体上隆起的一块硬或圆形的肿大部位
senses.example: She found a small lump on her arm and had it checked.
senses.exampleCN: 她发现手臂上有个小肿块，就去做了检查。
senses.why: A swelling has the same outline as a mass of clay or coal, so the body borrows the word for anything that pushes up under the skin.
senses.whyCN: 肿块与一团黏土或煤块的轮廓相同，于是身体借用了这个词，指任何在皮下顶起来的东西。

senses.title: To group things into one mass
senses.definition: to put separate people or things into one group without sorting them
senses.definitionCN: 把分开的人或物不加区分地放进同一组
senses.example: The report lumps all the small shops together as one category.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告把所有小店归并成同一类。
senses.why: If separate pieces are thrown into one pile, their edges disappear into a single mass; the verb is that throwing, applied to facts and categories.
senses.whyCN: 如果把分开的块丢进同一堆，它们的边就消失在一整团里；动词就是这一「丢」，只是对象换成了事实与类别。

senses.title: To accept something unpleasant
senses.definition: to swallow an unpleasant situation because it cannot be changed
senses.definitionCN: 因为无法改变而把不愉快的处境硬吞下去
senses.example: He did not like the decision, but he had to lump it.
senses.exampleCN: 他不喜欢这个决定，但也只能忍着接受。
senses.why: The phrase like it or lump it pictures the bad news as one hard lump that must be swallowed whole, since there is no way to chew it into smaller pieces.
senses.whyCN: like it or lump it 把坏消息想成一整块硬东西：既然没法嚼碎，就只能整块吞下。

intro.en: Lump is a Middle English noun for a shapeless mass; its deeper origin is uncertain, and the verb and medical senses grew from that solid block.
intro.cn: lump 是中古英语中表示「无定形一块」的名词；它更早的来源不确定，动词义与医学义都是从这块固体生长出来的。

items.en: The noun lump, also written lompe, first names a shapeless mass of material, neither shaped nor measured.
items.cn: 名词 lump 也写作 lompe，最初指一块既无形状也无定量的材料。

items.en: A common suggestion compares Middle Dutch lomp, a rag or a clumsy piece, and German Lumpen, a rag; the comparison is offered as possible, not as settled.
items.cn: 一种常见说法把它与中古荷兰语 lomp（破布、笨重的一块）和德语 Lumpen（破布）相比较；这只是一条可能的线索，并非定论。

items.en: The verb appears with the sense of throwing separate things into one mass, which gives phrases such as lump together and later lump sum.
items.cn: 动词义出现，意思是把分开的东西丢成一整堆，由此产生 lump together 以及后来的 lump sum 等说法。

items.en: Medical writers use lump for a swelling felt under the skin, and the same outline produces the phrase a lump in the throat for strong emotion.
items.cn: 医学作者用 lump 指皮下摸到的肿块；同样的轮廓又产生 a lump in the throat 这一说法，用来形容情绪激动。

items.en: Phrases such as take one's lumps and like it or lump it keep the sense of a hard thing that simply has to be borne.
items.cn: take one's lumps 与 like it or lump it 之类的说法，保留了「一块硬东西只能硬扛」的含义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms and derivatives built on lump; the near-meaning group gathers words for masses, pieces and swellings.
note.cn: 形近组收由 lump 构成的变形与派生词；近义组收表示块状物、团块与肿起的词。

normalIntro.en: The word begins as the name of a shapeless mass, and its family keeps returning to hard pieces, swellings and things thrown into one pile.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词起初是一团无定形材料的名字，同族词反复回到硬块、肿起以及被丢成一堆的东西。

normal.en: Lump is first a noun for a shapeless mass; the verb comes later and means to throw separate things into one pile.
normal.cn: lump 首先是名词，指无定形的一团；动词义较晚出现，意思是把分开的东西丢成一堆。

normal.en: Lump together keeps that picture: separate pieces lose their edges once they are dropped into the same heap.
normal.cn: lump together 保留了这个画面：分开的块一旦被丢进同一堆，就失去了各自的边。

normal.en: A lump of sugar is a small pressed block, which shows how loose the word is about exact shape.
normal.cn: 一块方糖就是压成的小方块，可见这个词对具体形状并不严格。

normal.en: A lump on the arm is a swelling shaped like a mass under the skin, so the medical sense borrows the physical one.
normal.cn: 手臂上的肿块就是皮下形似一团的东西，医学义直接借用了物理义。

normal.en: Like it or lump it means swallow the bad news whole, as if it were one hard lump with no way to chew it.
normal.cn: like it or lump it 意为把坏消息整块吞下，好像那是一块没法嚼的硬东西。

abstract.en: A lump has no edges to hold, which is why the word suits anything we cannot easily take apart.
abstract.cn: 一块 lump 没有可抓的棱角，所以这个词适合形容任何我们难以拆开的东西。

abstract.en: To lump people together is to lose the outlines that made them separate, and that is exactly the harm the verb describes.
abstract.cn: 把人 lump together，就是丢掉让他们彼此分开的轮廓，而这正是这个动词所指的害处。

abstract.en: A hard lump can be swallowed but not digested, which is a fair picture of a truth we accept without liking.
abstract.cn: 硬块吞得下却消化不了，这正好形容我们接受却并不喜欢的真相。

definition_zh: 肺；肺脏；呼吸能力；（城市的）绿肺
definition_en: one of the two organs in the chest used for breathing, the pair taken as the source of breath and voice, or a place imagined as the breathing organ of a city
core_image: 胸腔里两片粉红色的海绵，随着吸气慢慢张开
scene: 体检室里，医生把听诊器贴在少年背部，让他深吸一口气再慢慢吐出。The doctor listened to her lungs and asked her to breathe in again.
sceneCN: 这里 lung 是「肺」（第 1 个义项：胸腔里用于呼吸的器官）；句意为医生听了听她的两肺，又让她再吸一口气。图中可辨识物件：体检室、听诊器、少年的背部。

senses.title: The breathing organ in the chest
senses.definition: either of the two soft organs in the chest through which air passes and oxygen enters the blood
senses.definitionCN: 胸腔中两个柔软器官之一，空气经过其中，氧气由此进入血液
senses.example: The doctor listened to her lungs and asked her to breathe in again.
senses.exampleCN: 医生听了听她的两肺，又让她再吸一口气。
senses.why: The word names the organ by what it does with air: a bag inside the chest that fills and empties with every breath.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是按器官「对空气做了什么」来命名的：胸腔里一只随每次呼吸鼓起又排空的袋子。

senses.title: Breath and voice power
senses.definition: the strength of breath that supports a loud sound or long effort, usually spoken of as the lungs
senses.definitionCN: 支撑大声或长时间用力时的那股气息，通常以复数 lungs 表示
senses.example: She sang the last note at the top of her lungs.
senses.exampleCN: 她用尽全身力气唱出了最后一个音。
senses.why: Because a voice is pushed out by air from the lungs, the organ name becomes a way of saying how much breath and force a person has.
senses.whyCN: 声音靠肺里的气推出来，于是器官的名称变成了衡量一个人气息与力气的说法。

senses.title: A green space imagined as a city's lungs
senses.definition: a large park or belt of trees described as the part that freshens the air of a city
senses.definitionCN: 被形容为替城市更新空气的大片公园或林带
senses.example: The old park is called the lungs of the city.
senses.exampleCN: 这座老公园被称为城市的绿肺。
senses.why: A park does for a city what lungs do for a body: it takes in air and gives it back cleaner, so the organ is used as a figure for green space.
senses.whyCN: 公园对城市所做的事，正像肺对身体所做的事：吸入空气再还回更干净的空气，于是这个器官被用作绿地的比喻。

intro.en: Lung is an Old English word of Germanic stock, and it is generally linked to a root meaning light, because the organ is light enough to float.
intro.cn: lung 是源自日耳曼语族的古英语词，一般认为与表示「轻」的词根有关，因为肺轻得能浮在水上。

items.en: Old English lungen names the organ, and its plural already points to the pair inside the chest.
items.cn: 古英语 lungen 就是这个器官的名称，它的复数形式已经指向胸腔里的那对器官。

items.en: The reconstructed Germanic form is generally connected with a root meaning light in weight, because lungs are the lightest organs and float on water; most handbooks accept the link, though it is not certain.
items.cn: 重构的日耳曼语形式一般认为与表示「重量轻」的词根有关，因为肺是最轻的器官，能在水上浮起；多数词源手册接受这条联系，但它并非定论。

items.en: German Lunge, Dutch long and Swedish lunga keep the same shape, which is why the word looks so unlike Latin pulmo.
items.cn: 德语 Lunge、荷兰语 long 与瑞典语 lunga 保持同样的形状，所以这个词与拉丁语 pulmo 看起来毫不相干。

items.en: Middle English shortens the form to lunge and lunges, and the plural lungs becomes the usual way to speak of the pair.
items.cn: 中古英语把词形缩短为 lunge 与 lunges，复数 lungs 成为指这一对器官的通常说法。

items.en: Modern English adds two figures: the lungs as the source of a loud voice, and a park described as the lungs of a city.
items.cn: 现代英语添了两个比喻：肺是洪亮声音的来源，而公园被称为城市的肺。

note.cn: 形近组收复数形式与由 lung 构成的英语复合词；近义组收表示呼吸器官与气息的词。

entries.definitionCN: 鳃；鱼在水中取氧的器官，与肺相对。

entries.definitionCN: 气管；连接喉与肺的管道，不是肺本身。

entries.definitionCN: 胸部；容纳肺的部位，范围比肺大。

entries.definitionCN: 气息；指进出肺的空气本身，不指器官。

normalIntro.en: The word is an Old English organ name tied to lightness, and its family keeps returning to air, breath and the power of a voice.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是古英语的器官名，与「轻」有关；同族词反复回到空气、气息与声音的力量。

normal.en: Old English lungen named the organ, and every Germanic language keeps a close form: German Lunge, Dutch long, Swedish lunga.
normal.cn: 古英语 lungen 就是这个器官的名字，日耳曼各语都保留着很接近的形式：德语 Lunge、荷兰语 long、瑞典语 lunga。

normal.en: The name is generally tied to the Germanic word for light, because lungs are the lightest organs and float on water.
normal.cn: 这个名字一般认为与日耳曼语中表示「轻」的词有关，因为肺是最轻的器官，能在水上浮起。

normal.en: The plural lungs is the usual form for the pair, which is why at the top of one's lungs means with the force of both.
normal.cn: 指这一对器官时通常用复数 lungs，所以「at the top of one's lungs」意为用尽两肺的力气。

normal.en: Lungful adds -ful: the amount of air the lungs can take in at one breath.
normal.cn: lungful 在 lung 后加 -ful，指两肺一次能吸进的空气量。

normal.en: Lungfish are fish with an organ that works like a lung, so the compound joins two breathing worlds.
normal.cn: lungfish 是拥有类似肺的器官的鱼，这个复合词把两种呼吸方式连在一起。

abstract.en: A lung is a bag that must empty itself before it can fill, which makes breathing a lesson in letting go.
abstract.cn: 肺是一只必须先排空才能鼓起的袋子，于是呼吸本身成了「先放下」的一课。

abstract.en: Calling a park the lungs of a city admits that a city, like a body, cannot live on its own waste air.
abstract.cn: 把公园叫作城市的肺，等于承认城市也像身体一样，不能只靠自己呼出的浊气活着。

abstract.en: The organ named for lightness sits at the centre of the body, holding the air that every other organ depends on.
abstract.cn: 以「轻」命名的器官坐在身体中央，握着其他所有器官都依赖的那口气。

examples.en: Smoking damages the lungs over many years.
examples.cn: 吸烟会在多年间损伤两肺。

definition_zh: 奢侈；奢华；奢侈品；难得的享受；豪华的
definition_en: great comfort and expensive pleasure, a costly thing that is not necessary, a rare pleasure one allows oneself, or used before a noun for goods and places that are costly and high-grade
core_image: 橱窗里一只镶着金边的手袋，灯光把它照得像有温度
scene: 老城区的橱窗里摆着一只镶着金边的手袋，标价牌被灯光照得发亮。The shop window was filled with luxury goods that few people walking past could afford.
sceneCN: 这里 luxury 是「奢侈品」（第 2 个义项：并非必需而价格高昂的东西）；句意为橱窗里摆满了很少有人在路过时买得起的奢侈品。图中可辨识物件：老城区橱窗、镶金边的手袋、标价牌。

pos.zh: 奢侈；奢华；奢侈品；难得的享受

senses.title: Great comfort and costly pleasure
senses.definition: a style of life full of expensive comfort and pleasure, more than plain need requires
senses.definitionCN: 充满昂贵舒适与享乐的生活方式，远超朴素的需要
senses.example: They lived in luxury after the business took off.
senses.exampleCN: 生意兴隆之后，他们过上了奢华的生活。
senses.why: Latin luxuria named excess and rank growth; the modern sense keeps that image of something spilling past the limit of what is needed.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 luxuria 本指过度与繁茂的生长；现代义保留了「漫过所需限度」这一意象。

senses.title: A costly thing that is not necessary
senses.definition: an expensive object or service bought for pleasure rather than for need
senses.definitionCN: 为享乐而非为需要购买的昂贵物品或服务
senses.example: The watch is a luxury, not a necessity.
senses.exampleCN: 这块表是奢侈品，不是必需品。
senses.why: Once excess becomes a style of life, its objects can be counted one by one, so the abstract quality turns into things a person can own.
senses.whyCN: 一旦「过度」成为一种生活方式，它的物件就能一件件数出来，于是抽象的性质变成了可以拥有的具体东西。

senses.title: A rare pleasure one allows oneself
senses.titleCN: 难得的享受；小小的奢侈
senses.definition: something pleasant and not essential that a person allows themselves only now and then
senses.definitionCN: 令人愉快却并非必需、只偶尔允许自己享受的事物
senses.example: A long bath at the end of the week is a luxury.
senses.exampleCN: 周末结束时泡个长澡，是一种难得的享受。
senses.why: The word can shrink from a whole way of life to a single small indulgence, because the pleasure still costs more than ordinary routine would allow.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以从一整种生活方式缩小为一次小小的放纵，因为这份愉悦仍然比日常惯例所允许的更费钱费力。

senses.title: Costly and high-grade, before a noun
senses.definition: used before a noun for goods, travel or housing that are expensive and meant to feel superior
senses.definitionCN: 用于名词之前，指昂贵且刻意营造高级感的商品、旅行或住宅
senses.example: They booked a luxury suite for the anniversary.
senses.exampleCN: 他们为纪念日订了一间豪华套房。
senses.why: English often turns a noun of excess into a label placed before another noun, so the thing being sold carries the promise of the whole category.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把表示过度的名词变成放在另一名词前的标签，于是被出售的东西就带上了整个类别的承诺。

intro.en: Luxury comes from Latin luxus and luxuria, words for excess and profusion, which passed through Old French luxurie before English used it for costly comfort.
intro.cn: luxury 来自拉丁语 luxus 与 luxuria，意为过度与繁盛；它经古法语 luxurie 进入英语，后来才指昂贵的舒适。

items.en: Luxus names excess, extravagance and lavish display; a second Latin sense, a dislocation or displacement, is sometimes linked to it, but the relation between the two is debated.
items.cn: luxus 指过度、奢靡与铺张的展示；拉丁语中它另有一个「错位、脱节」的义项，有人把两者联系起来，但二者关系仍有争论。

items.en: Luxuria, built on luxus, means excess and profusion, and it also describes the rank, over-lush growth of plants.
items.cn: 由 luxus 构成的 luxuria 意为过度与繁盛，也用来描述植物疯长、过于茂密的生长。

items.en: Old French luxurie carries the word into English with a moral tone, meaning lust and dissolute living.
items.cn: 古法语 luxurie 带着道德评判把这词带进英语，意为淫欲与放荡的生活。

items.en: In Middle English luxurie is first a vice of excess, and only later does it drift towards costly comfort.
items.cn: 在中古英语里，luxurie 起初是一种过度放纵的恶习，后来才慢慢转向昂贵的舒适。

items.en: By the eighteenth century luxury has lost much of its moral sting, and in the twentieth century it also works as an adjective before nouns such as hotel and suite.
items.cn: 到十八世纪，luxury 的道德锋芒已大大减弱；到二十世纪，它还能作形容词放在 hotel、suite 这类名词之前。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the Latin-stem family of adjectives and adverbs; the near-meaning group gathers words for wealth, excess and comfort.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁词干上的形容词与副词；近义组收表示财富、过度与舒适的词。

entries.definition: Very comfortable and costly, as a room, a car or a life.
entries.definitionCN: 同一拉丁词干构成的形容词，义为「奢华的；豪华的」。

entries.definition: In a costly and comfortable manner.
entries.definitionCN: 由 luxurious 加 -ly 构成，义为「奢华地」。

entries.definition: Growing thickly and richly, used of hair, plants or style.
entries.definitionCN: 同一词干的形容词，义为「茂盛的；丰富的」，偏指生长繁密。

entries.definition: The quality of growing thickly or being richly abundant.
entries.definitionCN: 同一词干的名词，义为「繁茂；丰盛」。

entries.definition: Great wealth shown openly in costly things and surroundings.
entries.definitionCN: 富裕；强调公开显示的财富与排场，比 luxury 更偏炫耀。

entries.definition: Spending more than is reasonable or necessary.
entries.definitionCN: 铺张；强调花费超出合理或必需，带批评色彩。

entries.definition: A pleasant state of ease without effort or pain.
entries.definitionCN: 舒适；只强调身心的安逸，不含昂贵之意。

entries.definition: Impressive and expensive beauty, especially of a place.
entries.definitionCN: 辉煌；强调视觉上的华美与气派，多用于场所。

normalIntro.en: The word goes back to Latin nouns for excess, and its family keeps returning to lavishness, growth beyond bounds and costly comfort.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词上溯到表示过度的拉丁名词，同族词反复回到奢靡、越界生长与昂贵的舒适。

normal.en: Luxury goes back to Latin luxus, excess, so the word still carries the idea of more than need requires.
normal.cn: luxury 上溯到拉丁语 luxus（过度），所以这个词仍带着「超出所需」的意思。

normal.en: Latin luxuria also named the rank growth of plants, so lavishness and a plant spilling past its bounds share one picture.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 luxuria 也指植物疯长，所以铺张与植物漫出边界共享同一幅画面。

normal.en: Luxurious, luxuriant and luxury share one stem, but luxurious describes costly comfort while luxuriant describes thick growth.
normal.cn: luxurious、luxuriant 与 luxury 共用一个词干，但 luxurious 指昂贵的舒适，luxuriant 指茂密的生长。

normal.en: The French form luxurie came into English with a moral sting, meaning dissolute living before it meant fine things.
normal.cn: 法语形式 luxurie 带着道德批评进入英语，先指放荡的生活，后来才指精美的东西。

normal.en: In the lap of luxury is the fixed phrase for a life surrounded by costly comfort.
normal.cn: in the lap of luxury 是形容生活被昂贵舒适包围的固定说法。

abstract.en: A word born from excess suggests that luxury is defined not by objects but by the line they cross.
abstract.cn: 一个从「过度」中诞生的词说明，奢侈不由物品定义，而由它越过的界线定义。

abstract.en: The same root grows plants and sells suites, which is why richness always looks like something spilling over its edges.
abstract.cn: 同一个词根既让植物疯长，也用来卖套房，所以「丰盛」总像某种漫出边缘的东西。

abstract.en: Luxury is what comfort becomes when it stops answering a need and starts answering a desire.
abstract.cn: 奢侈就是舒适不再回应需要、转而回应欲望时的样子。

examples.en: The shop window was filled with luxury goods that few people walking past could afford.
examples.cn: 橱窗里摆满了很少有人在路过时买得起的奢侈品。

examples.en: They lived in luxury after the business took off.
examples.cn: 生意兴隆之后，他们过上了奢华的生活。

examples.en: They booked a luxury suite for the anniversary.
examples.cn: 他们为纪念日订了一间豪华套房。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「乐奢瑞」——日子过得乐、又舍得奢，才叫 luxury；记住它是奢侈、奢华。

root: 拉丁语 luxus（过度、奢靡）与 luxuria（过量、繁茂的生长）经古法语 luxurie 进入英语；一般认为核心是「超出限度」，luxus 两义之间的关系学界仍有争论；luxurious、luxuriant 都从这一词干而来。

sensesIntro.en: The core is excess beyond need; the senses divide into a lavish way of life, costly objects, a small rare indulgence, and the adjective for high-grade goods.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是超出所需的过度；义项由此分出奢华的生活方式、昂贵的物件、偶尔的小小放纵，以及指高级商品的形容词用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a gold-trimmed handbag in a shop window, lit until it seems warm.
core.cn: 核心意象：橱窗里一只镶着金边的手袋，灯光把它照得像有温度。

branches.en: a house kept far larger than the family needs
branches.cn: 一所远超家庭所需的房子

branches.en: a gold-trimmed bag behind lit glass
branches.cn: 灯光玻璃柜后镶金边的手袋

branches.en: a long bath taken without hurry
branches.cn: 不慌不忙泡的一个长澡

branches.en: a hotel door held open by a doorman
branches.cn: 门童替你拉开的酒店大门

branches.en: a price tag turned towards the light
branches.cn: 被转向灯光的标价牌

intro.en: The word is a Latin stem of excess with a French ending; its family adds the suffixes -ous and -ly to build the adjective and the adverb.
intro.cn: 这个词是表示过度的拉丁词干加上法语词尾；它的同族词加 -ous 与 -ly 构成形容词与副词。

latinIntro.en: Luxury has a recorded Latin family: luxus, luxuria and luxuriosus all belong to the same stem of excess and profusion.
latinIntro.cn: luxury 有可靠的拉丁同族词：luxus、luxuria 与 luxuriosus 都属于表示过度与繁盛的同一词干。

items.meaning: costly comfort or a costly thing
items.example: The suite was pure luxury.
items.exampleCN: 这间套房是纯粹的奢华。

items.meaningCN: 构成表示「充满……」的形容词后缀
