items.example: The garden was luxuriant after the rains.
items.exampleCN: 雨后花园一片茂盛。

definition_zh: 机器；由部件组成并做功的装置；也指计算机或组织化的运作体系；动词指机械加工
definition_en: a device of connected parts that performs work; also a computer or an organised system, and to cut or shape with a machine tool
core_image: 一台车床夹着一段金属，刀头沿着导轨推进，铁屑卷成一圈圈落下来
scene: 车间的车床夹着一段金属，刀头沿导轨推进，铁屑卷成一圈圈落下。The machine cut the shaft to within a hair of the required size.
sceneCN: 这里 machine 指由部件组成并做功的装置（第 1 个义项：机器这一装置）；句意：这台机器把轴削到与要求尺寸相差不到一根头发；对应第 1 个义项。

senses.title: A device that performs work
senses.definition: an assembly of connected parts that uses power to carry out a task
senses.definitionCN: 由相连部件构成、使用动力完成任务的组合体
senses.example: The machine lifts the load with a single lever.
senses.exampleCN: 这台机器只用一个手柄就抬起货物。
senses.why: the Greek noun named any contrivance, so the first sense is the broad one of a built device.
senses.whyCN: 希腊名词原指任何巧妙装置，因此第一个义项就是「人造装置」这一宽泛含义。

senses.title: A computer
senses.definition: the computing hardware that executes stored instructions
senses.definitionCN: 执行已存指令的计算硬件
senses.example: The machine rebooted before the backup finished.
senses.exampleCN: 备份还没完成，机器就重启了。
senses.why: computers became the most common machine in daily life, and speakers shortened the name.
senses.whyCN: 计算机成了日常最常见的机器，说话者就把名称缩短了。

senses.title: A household or workshop appliance
senses.definition: a named device for one task, as in a washing or sewing machine
senses.definitionCN: 为单一任务命名的装置，如洗衣机或缝纫机
senses.example: The sewing machine has outlived three owners.
senses.exampleCN: 那台缝纫机已经比三位主人活得都久。
senses.why: a device is named by its task plus this general word, which is how the compound names spread.
senses.whyCN: 装置以「任务＋这个总称」命名，这类复合名称就是这样扩散的。

senses.title: A machine tool
senses.definition: a powered tool that cuts or shapes metal and other materials
senses.definitionCN: 切削或成型金属等材料的动力工具
senses.example: The new machine holds a tolerance of a hundredth of a millimetre.
senses.exampleCN: 这台新机床能保持百分之一毫米的公差。
senses.why: in a workshop, the general word often means the tool that makes other parts.
senses.whyCN: 在车间里，这个总称常指制造其他零件的工具。

senses.title: To cut or shape by machine
senses.definition: to remove material or form a part with a powered tool
senses.definitionCN: 用动力工具去除材料或成型零件
senses.example: They machined the block in two passes.
senses.exampleCN: 他们分两道工序加工了那块坯料。
senses.why: the noun became a verb the moment the tool's action needed a name.
senses.whyCN: 当工具的动作需要一个名称时，名词就变成了动词。

senses.title: A political organisation
senses.definition: the permanent staff and structure that win elections or hold power
senses.definitionCN: 赢得选举或维持权力的常设人员与结构
senses.example: The party machine decided the candidate before the vote.
senses.exampleCN: 政党机器在投票之前就决定了候选人。
senses.why: an organisation that runs without sentiment is described by the most impersonal noun available.
senses.whyCN: 不带感情运转的组织，就用最非人格的名词来描述。

senses.title: An impersonal system of rule
senses.definition: the administrative apparatus of a state or large institution
senses.definitionCN: 国家或大型机构的行政装置
senses.example: The state machine ground down every small request.
senses.exampleCN: 国家机器把每一个小请求都磨掉了。
senses.why: the image of interlocking parts describes bureaucracy better than any abstract word.
senses.whyCN: 「咬合的部件」这一意象，比任何抽象词都更能描述官僚体系。

senses.title: A person who acts automatically
senses.definition: a person treated as incapable of independent thought
senses.definitionCN: 被视为无法独立思考的人
senses.example: They turned him into a machine that answered tickets.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把他变成一台只回答工单的机器。
senses.why: calling a person a machine denies judgement, which is the insult the word carries here.
senses.whyCN: 把人叫作机器就是否认其判断力，这正是这个词在此处的贬义。

senses.title: Automated by computation
senses.definition: used before a noun for processes carried out by computers
senses.definitionCN: 用在名词前，指由计算机完成的过程
senses.example: Machine translation improved, but it still misses tone.
senses.exampleCN: 机器翻译进步了，却仍抓不住语气。
senses.why: as a modifier, the word marks the shift from human to computed action.
senses.whyCN: 作修饰语时，这个词标记从人工到计算动作的转移。

senses.title: The power unit of a vehicle
senses.definition: the engine and its housing in a boat, train or vehicle
senses.definitionCN: 船、火车或车辆中的发动机及其外壳
senses.example: The fire machine kept its pump running for nine hours.
senses.exampleCN: 消防车的泵持续运转了九个小时。
senses.why: early industrial English called a powered vehicle a machine, and the usage survives in a few names.
senses.whyCN: 早期工业英语把动力车辆叫作 machine，这种用法在少数名称里留存下来。

intro.en: Machine came from Greek mekhane through Latin machina and French. It meant any contrivance long before it meant a powered device, and its computing and organisational senses are later extensions.
intro.cn: machine 经拉丁语 machina 与法语来自希腊语 mekhane。它很久以前指任何巧妙装置，之后才指动力装置；计算机义与组织义是更晚的延伸。

items.en: Greek mekhane named a device, especially a stage crane or a siege engine, and also a means or expedient.
items.cn: 希腊语 mekhane 指装置，尤指舞台吊机或攻城器械，也指手段与办法。

items.en: Latin machina meant a structure, scaffold or engine, and the phrase deus ex machina came from the stage crane.
items.cn: 拉丁语 machina 指结构、脚手架或器械，短语 deus ex machina 就来自舞台吊机。

items.en: French machine entered English in the seventeenth century and covered any constructed device, not only powered ones.
items.cn: 法语 machine 在十七世纪进入英语，指任何建造出来的装置，而不只是动力装置。

items.en: Steam and factory work narrowed machine toward devices with moving parts driven by power.
items.cn: 蒸汽与工厂作业把 machine 收窄为由动力驱动、带运动部件的装置。

items.en: The twentieth century added the computer and the party machine, both built on the image of parts working together.
items.cn: 二十世纪加上计算机与政党机器两义，二者都建立在「部件协同运转」的意象上。

items.en: Machining arose in workshops as the verb for what a machine tool does to metal.
items.cn: machining 在车间里产生，指机床对金属所做的加工。

note.en: The first group is the machine family in other shapes; the second group is the neighbouring words for devices and systems.
note.cn: 第一组是 machine 词族的其他形态；第二组是装置与体系的相邻说法。

entries.definition: Machines as a mass; one machine is countable, machinery is not.
entries.definitionCN: 指机器的整体；一台机器可数，machinery 不可数。

entries.definition: A person who operates or makes machines; the noun names the equipment.
entries.definitionCN: 指操作或制造机器的人；名词指设备。

entries.definition: A person who repairs machines; a machine is the thing repaired.
entries.definitionCN: 指修理机器的人；machine 是被修的东西。

entries.definition: The set of parts that produces a motion; a machine contains one or more mechanisms.
entries.definitionCN: 指产生运动的那组部件；一台机器包含一个或多个机构。

entries.definition: Any constructed thing made for a purpose, often small; a machine usually has moving parts and power.
entries.definitionCN: 为某目的造的任何东西，常指小型；machine 通常有运动部件与动力。

entries.definition: A machine that converts energy into motion; it is a part of many machines.
entries.definitionCN: 把能量转成运动的机器；它是许多机器的一个部件。

entries.definition: An implement a person holds and guides; a machine supplies its own motion.
entries.definitionCN: 由人握持与引导的器具；machine 自己提供运动。

entries.definition: A set of equipment working as one, often for an experiment or an institution.
entries.definitionCN: 作为整体工作的一整套设备，常用于实验或机构。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations from the real Greek source and the real noun-verb pair.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：来自真实希腊语来源与真实名词动词成对关系。

normal.en: Mekhane meant a stage crane, so a machine is first a thing that lifts and moves.
normal.cn: mekhane 原指舞台吊机，所以 machine 首先是能吊起与移动东西的装置。

normal.en: The verb forms are regular: machines, machined, machined, machining.
normal.cn: 动词形式规则：machines、machined、machined、machining。

normal.en: Task names build on it: washing machine, sewing machine, machine tool.
normal.cn: 任务名称在它之上构成：洗衣机、缝纫机、机床。

normal.en: The computing sense is simply the shortened name of the most common machine.
normal.cn: 计算机义不过是「最常用机器」的简称。

normal.en: Two objects split the verb: machine a part, machine a surface.
normal.cn: 两类宾语分开动词：加工一个零件，加工一个表面。

abstract.en: Picture a crane on a stage lowering a god who is only a painted board.
abstract.cn: 想象舞台上的吊机放下一个神，而那神不过是一块画板。

abstract.en: Picture a lathe turning a shaft until the metal is exactly the size of an idea.
abstract.cn: 想象车床削一根轴，直到金属恰好等于一个想法的尺寸。

abstract.en: Picture an office where every request disappears into a slot and comes out stamped.
abstract.cn: 想象一间办公室，每个请求都落进一个槽口，再盖着章出来。

examples.en: The machine does the lifting, but a person still chooses where.
examples.cn: 机器负责起吊，但选择吊到哪里仍由人决定。

examples.en: They machined the replacement part overnight.
examples.cn: 他们连夜加工了那只替换零件。

examples.en: The party machine had chosen the nominee months earlier.
examples.cn: 政党机器几个月前就已定下候选人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「马（ma）身（chine）」——马拉着的一副身架，就是最早干活的机器

root: 希腊 mekhane「装置、舞台吊机」→ 拉丁 machina「结构、器械」→ 法语 machine → 英语 machine；先泛指装置，工业时代收窄为动力装置，二十世纪扩展出计算机与组织体系义，动词指机床加工。

sensesIntro.en: Ten senses run from the general device to the computer, the appliance, the machine tool, the verb, the party machine, the state apparatus, the dehumanised person, computed processes and the vehicle's power unit.
sensesIntro.cn: 十个义项从泛指的装置出发，经过计算机、家用器具、机床、动词用法、政党机器、国家机器、被机械化的人、计算化流程，最后到车辆动力机组。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lathe holding a metal shaft while a cutter advances and curls off chips.
core.cn: 核心意象：车床夹着一段金属轴，刀头推进，铁屑卷曲落下。

branches.en: DEVICES: any working assembly, and the named appliance built on that pattern.
branches.cn: 装置：任何做功的组合体，以及按此模式命名的器具。

branches.en: COMPUTATION: the computer itself, and processes carried out by computed action.
branches.cn: 计算：计算机本身，以及由计算动作完成的过程。

branches.en: TOOL AND ACTION: the machine tool, and the verb for what it does to metal.
branches.cn: 工具与动作：机床，以及它对金属所做加工的动词。

branches.en: ORGANISED POWER: the party machine, and the administrative apparatus of a state.
branches.cn: 组织化的权力：政党机器，以及国家的行政装置。

branches.en: THE MECHANICAL FIGURE: a person reduced to a machine, and a vehicle's engine unit.
branches.cn: 机械化的形象：被降为机器的人，以及车辆的动力机组。

intro.en: Machine is a borrowed noun with no living affix; its family adds -ery, -ist, -ing and compound forms.
intro.cn: machine 是借入名词，本身没有能产的词缀；其词族另加 -ery、-ist、-ing 与复合形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin machina is the direct source of the French and English forms; the Greek noun mekhane stands behind it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 machina 是法语与英语形式的直接来源，其背后是希腊名词 mekhane。

items.example: The Greek noun carries both the machine and the trick.
items.exampleCN: 这个希腊名词兼有「机器」与「计策」两面。

items.example: Latin widened the noun to any built structure.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语把这个名词扩大到任何建造的结构。

items.meaning: device; to cut with a tool
items.example: English uses the same form for the object and the action.
items.exampleCN: 英语用同一形式指对象与动作。

items.example: The ending produces the uncountable collective.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾产生不可数的集合名词。

items.example: The ending names the operator.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾指操作者。

items.example: The ending names the cutting work itself.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾指切削工作本身。

items.example: The ending marks what a device can read or do.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾标记装置能读或能做的事。

items.example: The ending names one arrangement of moving parts.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾指一套运动部件的组合。

definition_zh: 机械；机器的总称；也指机构或运作体系
definition_en: machines taken as a group, or the working parts of a system, including an organisation's apparatus
core_image: 一排机器连着同一条传动轴，皮带一起转动，整片地面都在轻微震动
scene: 车间里一排机器连着同一条传动轴，皮带一齐转动，整片地面都在轻轻震动。The factory replaced its old machinery with one quieter line.
sceneCN: 这里 machinery 指机器的总称（第 1 个义项：成套机器）；句意：工厂把旧机械换成了一条更安静的产线；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 机械（总称）；机器部件；机构

senses.title: Machines as a collective body
senses.definition: a group of machines considered together, especially in a workplace
senses.definitionCN: 被一并看待的一组机器，尤指工作场所中的
senses.example: The plant bought new machinery before hiring new staff.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂先买新机械，再招新员工。
senses.why: the -ery ending makes a mass noun, so the word names machines as a body rather than one machine.
senses.whyCN: -ery 词尾构成集合名词，因此这个词指一批机器，而不是一台机器。

senses.title: The working parts inside a machine
senses.definition: the internal parts that transmit motion in a device
senses.definitionCN: 在装置内部传递运动的部件
senses.example: The clock's machinery needed oil, not a new face.
senses.exampleCN: 这座钟的机械部件需要上油，而不是换表盘。
senses.why: the collective noun also covers the parts that make one machine work, since they too are a set.
senses.whyCN: 集合名词也指使单台机器运转的那组部件，因为它们同样成组。

senses.title: The apparatus of an organisation
senses.definition: the people, offices and procedures that keep an institution running
senses.definitionCN: 维持一个机构运转的人员、部门与程序
senses.example: Reform stalled inside the machinery of the ministry.
senses.exampleCN: 改革在部委的机构内部停住了。
senses.why: an organisation works through parts that transmit decisions, exactly as gears transmit motion.
senses.whyCN: 组织靠传递决定的部件运作，正如齿轮传递运动。

senses.title: A process treated as a system
senses.titleCN: 被当作系统看待的流程
senses.definition: the arrangeable steps by which something is carried out
senses.definitionCN: 完成某事时可加以安排的那些步骤
senses.example: The machinery of appeal is slow but predictable.
senses.exampleCN: 申诉的运作机制缓慢，却可预期。
senses.why: once steps are regular enough to be described, they can be spoken of as machinery.
senses.whyCN: 当步骤规律到可以被描述，人们就会把它说成机械装置。

senses.title: Farm equipment as a class
senses.definition: the tractors and implements used in farming, taken together
senses.definitionCN: 农业中使用的拖拉机与农具的总和
senses.example: Shared machinery let small farms afford a harvester.
senses.exampleCN: 共用机械让小农场也买得起收割机。
senses.why: the collective noun is the natural way to speak of a category of equipment bought and kept together.
senses.whyCN: 集合名词是谈论「成套购买与保管」的设备类别的自然方式。

senses.title: Stage and studio equipment
senses.definition: the rigging and devices that move scenery or sets
senses.definitionCN: 移动布景或场地的吊装与装置
senses.example: The theatre's machinery was hidden behind the curtain.
senses.exampleCN: 剧院的舞台机械藏在幕布之后。
senses.why: theatre has used hidden devices for centuries, and the collective word names them without exposure.
senses.whyCN: 剧院使用隐蔽装置已有数百年，集合名词正好不必把它们露出来。

senses.title: The mechanism of an abstract force
senses.definition: the system by which a large process such as war or law is conducted
senses.definitionCN: 战争或法律等大型过程得以进行的系统
senses.example: The machinery of war outlived the government that built it.
senses.exampleCN: 战争的机器比建立它的政府活得更久。
senses.why: the figurative use extends to anything vast, impersonal and hard to stop.
senses.whyCN: 比喻用法延伸到一切庞大、非人格且难以停止的事物。

senses.title: Heavy equipment on a site
senses.definition: the excavators and cranes that do the heavy physical work
senses.definitionCN: 从事繁重体力作业的挖掘机与起重机
senses.example: Heavy machinery arrived before the surveyors finished.
senses.exampleCN: 重型机械在测量员完工之前就进场了。
senses.why: on a site, the word means the class of large powered equipment, not a single tool.
senses.whyCN: 在工地上，这个词指大型动力设备这一类别，而不是单件工具。

intro.en: Machinery is a collective noun built on machine, which comes from Greek mekhane through Latin machina and French. The -ery ending turns one device into a body of devices.
intro.cn: machinery 是在 machine 上构成的集合名词，而 machine 经拉丁语 machina 与法语来自希腊语 mekhane。-ery 词尾把一台装置变成一批装置。

items.en: Greek mekhane meant a device, an engine of war or a means of doing something.
items.cn: 希腊语 mekhane 指装置、攻城器械或做事的手段。

items.en: Latin machina named a structure, scaffold or engine, and kept the Greek sense of a contrivance.
items.cn: 拉丁语 machina 指结构、脚手架或器械，保留了希腊语「巧妙装置」的意思。

items.en: French machine carried the word into English in the seventeenth century, at first for any structure or device.
items.cn: 法语 machine 在十七世纪把这个词带入英语，最初指任何结构或装置。

items.en: English machine narrowed toward powered devices as steam and industry spread.
items.cn: 随着蒸汽与工业扩散，英语 machine 逐渐收窄为动力装置。

items.en: The ending -ery, from French -erie, gathers things into a mass or a trade, giving machinery, cutlery and stationery.
items.cn: 词尾 -ery 来自法语 -erie，把事物聚成整体或行业，形成 machinery、cutlery、stationery 这类词。

items.en: Bureaucracy and warfare gave the collective word its modern figurative sense of an impersonal working system.
items.cn: 官僚制度与战争给了这个集合词现代比喻义：非人格的运作系统。

note.en: The first group is the machine root in different shapes and counts; the second group is the neighbouring collective and system words.
note.cn: 第一组是「机器」词根的不同形态与单复数；第二组是相邻的集合与系统说法。

entries.definition: A single device; machinery is the mass of such devices, so it takes no plural.
entries.definitionCN: 指单台装置；machinery 是这类装置的整体，因此没有复数。

entries.definition: The person who runs a machine; the collective noun names the equipment, not the worker.
entries.definitionCN: 指操作机器的人；集合名词指设备，不指工人。

entries.definition: A particular arrangement of parts that produces motion; machinery is the wider set.
entries.definitionCN: 指产生运动的某套部件组合；machinery 是更大的集合。

entries.definition: Of machines or done without thought; the noun machinery carries only the equipment sense.
entries.definitionCN: 指机器的或不假思索的；名词 machinery 只保留设备义。

entries.definition: Any set of items needed for a purpose; machinery is specifically powered machines.
entries.definitionCN: 为某目的所需的一整套物件；machinery 特指动力机器。

entries.definition: A set of parts working together for a function, often in science or politics.
entries.definitionCN: 为一功能共同运作的一整套部件，常用于科学或政治语境。

entries.definition: An organised set of parts or steps; machinery is the concrete or institutional version.
entries.definitionCN: 有组织的部件或步骤集合；machinery 是其具体或建制化的版本。

entries.definition: The buildings and machines of an industrial site taken as one unit.
entries.definitionCN: 把一个工业场所的建筑与机器当作一个整体。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations from the real suffix and the real collective phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：来自真实词尾与真实集合搭配。

normal.en: The -ery ending makes a mass noun, as in cutlery and stationery.
normal.cn: -ery 词尾构成集合名词，如 cutlery、stationery。

normal.en: It takes no plural: one says much machinery, not many machineries.
normal.cn: 它没有复数：说 much machinery，而不说 many machineries。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: heavy machinery, agricultural machinery, industrial machinery.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：重型机械、农业机械、工业机械。

normal.en: The figurative sense needs a system: the machinery of government, the machinery of justice.
normal.cn: 比喻义要接一个体系：政府机构、司法机制。

normal.en: One machine is a machine; a hall full of them is machinery.
normal.cn: 一台叫 a machine，一屋子就是 machinery。

abstract.en: Picture a single shaft running through a whole hall, so that every machine turns at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一根轴穿过整个车间，于是所有机器同时转动。

abstract.en: Picture an office where decisions travel along belts nobody can see.
abstract.cn: 想象一间办公室，决定沿着看不见的皮带传递。

abstract.en: Picture stage rigging moving a forest while the audience watches only the forest.
abstract.cn: 想象舞台吊装移动整片树林，而观众只看见树林。

examples.en: The mill's machinery was older than any of its workers.
examples.cn: 这家磨坊的机械比它的任何工人都老。

examples.en: Agricultural machinery changed the size of the average field.
examples.cn: 农业机械改变了普通田块的大小。

examples.en: Reform required changing the machinery, not just the minister.
examples.cn: 改革需要更换机构本身，而不只是换部长。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「马（ma）先（chine）瑞（ry）」——马先拉动的这一整套东西，就是机械

root: 希腊 mekhane「装置」→ 拉丁 machina → 法语 machine → 英语 machine；加集合词尾 -ery（法语 -erie）构成 machinery，指成套机器，后引申指机构与运作体系。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from machines as a body to the parts inside one, then to organisational apparatus, processes, farm equipment, stage rigging, abstract systems and site equipment.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从成套机器出发，走向单台机器内部部件，再到组织机构、流程、农业装备、舞台吊装、抽象体系与工地设备。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of machines coupled to one shaft, belts turning together until the floor trembles.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排机器接到同一根轴上，皮带一齐转动，地板微微发颤。

branches.en: EQUIPMENT CLASSES: machines in general, farm equipment, and heavy site plant.
branches.cn: 设备类别：泛指的机器、农业装备，以及工地重型设备。

branches.en: INNER PARTS: the set of parts that makes one device move.
branches.cn: 内部部件：使单台装置运动的那组零件。

branches.en: INSTITUTIONAL APPARATUS: offices, staff and procedures that keep an organisation running.
branches.cn: 机构装置：维持组织运转的部门、人员与程序。

branches.en: PROCESS AS SYSTEM: regular steps that can be described and rearranged.
branches.cn: 作为系统的流程：可被描述与重排的规律步骤。

branches.en: HIDDEN AND VAST: stage rigging behind a curtain, and the mechanism of war or law.
branches.cn: 隐蔽与庞大：幕后的舞台吊装，以及战争或法律的运作机制。

intro.en: Machinery is machine with a collective ending; the base itself came into English through French from Latin.
intro.cn: machinery 是 machine 加集合词尾；其词基本身经法语从拉丁语进入英语。

latinIntro.en: Latin machina is the direct source of French machine; the collective ending -ery came separately through French -erie.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 machina 是法语 machine 的直接来源；集合词尾 -ery 另经法语 -erie 而来。

items.example: The Greek noun starts the chain of borrowings.
items.exampleCN: 这个希腊名词开启了一连串借入。

items.example: Latin passed the word to French unchanged in sense.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语几乎原样把词义传给法语。

items.example: The base is a count noun and takes a plural.
items.exampleCN: 这个词基是可数名词，有复数。

items.meaning: a body or trade of things
items.example: The ending gathers many machines into one mass.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把许多机器聚成一个整体。

items.example: The ending names the person who runs the equipment.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾指操作设备的人。

items.example: The ending builds the word for one assembly of parts.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾构成「一套部件组合」的词。

items.example: The base appears across the whole technical family.
items.exampleCN: 这个词基出现在整个技术词族中。

items.example: The ending produces the related adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾产生相关形容词。

definition_zh: 发疯的；精神失常的；生气的；恼火的；狂热的；痴迷的；愚蠢的
definition_en: suffering from a serious mental illness, extremely angry in everyday speech, wildly enthusiastic, or foolish beyond reason
core_image: 一个人对着空椅子认真争辩，眼里的世界与旁人看到的完全不同
scene: 夜里的急诊走廊上，一位老人对着空气大声争辩，护士轻声请来值班医生。The old man had gone mad and kept arguing with people who were not there.
sceneCN: 这里 mad 是「精神失常的、发疯的」（第 1 个义项：神志不清）；句意为老人已经疯了，一直跟并不存在的人争论。图中可辨识物件：急诊走廊的灯、护士站、病历夹。

pos.zh: 发疯的；精神失常的；生气的；狂热的；愚蠢的

collocations.zh: 彻底疯了；疯得不可理喻

derivatives.zh: 由 mad 加 -ness 构成，义为「疯狂；精神失常」
由 mad 加 -ly 构成，义为「疯狂地；非正式口语中作『极其』」
由 mad 与 man 复合，义为「疯子；失去理智的男人」

senses.title: Mentally ill and out of touch with reality
senses.definition: suffering from a serious mental illness, so that the person cannot think or behave as others do
senses.definitionCN: 患有严重精神疾病，思考和举止与常人不同
senses.example: The old man had been declared mad and could no longer live alone.
senses.exampleCN: 那位老人已被判定精神失常，再也不能独自生活。
senses.why: Old English gemǣd described a mind that had been altered out of its proper state, so illness of the mind is the oldest recorded sense of the word.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 gemǣd 描述的是神志被改变、脱离正常状态，所以「心智患病」是这个词最早的记录义项。

senses.title: Very angry
senses.definition: extremely annoyed about something, in everyday informal speech
senses.definitionCN: 在日常口语中因某事而极为恼火
senses.example: She was mad at me for forgetting her birthday.
senses.exampleCN: 她因为我不记得她的生日而生我的气。
senses.why: Anger was pictured as a passing disturbance of the mind, and the word for a disordered mind slid into the word for a hot temper.
senses.whyCN: 愤怒被想象成心智一时的失序，于是那个表示「头脑不正常」的词便滑向了「火气上来」这层意思。

senses.title: Wildly enthusiastic
senses.definition: so enthusiastic about someone or something that ordinary caution disappears
senses.definitionCN: 对某人或某物极为热衷，连平常的谨慎都没有了
senses.example: He is mad about vintage motorcycles and spends every weekend in the garage.
senses.exampleCN: 他痴迷老式摩托车，每个周末都泡在车库里。
senses.why: Enthusiasm that sweeps away caution looks like the same loss of control, so the word moved from illness and anger to passion.
senses.whyCN: 那种把谨慎一扫而空的热情，看上去是同一种失控，于是这个词从疾病、愤怒又走到了迷恋。

senses.title: Foolish and ill judged
senses.definition: wildly foolish, used of plans or actions that no sensible person would attempt
senses.definitionCN: 极其愚蠢的，用于形容任何明白人都不会尝试的计划或举动
senses.example: Crossing the river in that storm was a mad thing to do.
senses.exampleCN: 在那样一场暴风雨里过河，是件极其愚蠢的事。
senses.why: Before it named illness, the word already meant foolish, so poor judgement remains the quiet base under every later sense.
senses.whyCN: 在指疾病之前，这个词早已表示「愚蠢」，所以「判断力差」一直是后来各义项底下沉默的底色。

intro.en: Mad is an Old English word for a disordered mind; its later senses of anger and passion grew from that base, and its deeper root is debated.
intro.cn: mad 是古英语中表示「神志失常」的词；后来「愤怒」与「痴迷」的意思都从这个底子长出来，更早的语源仍有争论。

items.en: A reconstructed Germanic adjective, usually taken to mean changed or altered, and often explained as a mind shifted out of its normal state; the exact formation is uncertain.
items.cn: 一个重构的日耳曼语形容词，一般认为意为「被改变的」，常被解释为神志偏出了正常状态；确切构成仍不确定。

items.en: Gemǣd is recorded in Old English for foolish and insane, and the ge- prefix gathers the word into a completed state.
items.cn: gemǣd 在古英语中记录为愚蠢的、精神失常的，前缀 ge- 把词收进一种已完成的状态。

items.en: Middle English drops the prefix and keeps mad, and by the fourteenth century the word also means angrily excited.
items.cn: 中古英语去掉前缀，保留 mad；到十四世纪，这个词也指「怒气冲冲的」。

items.en: The phrases mad about and mad for come to mean passionately fond, first of people and then of pursuits.
items.cn: 短语 mad about 与 mad for 开始表示「极其喜爱」，先用于人，后用于嗜好。

items.en: Modern English keeps the medical sense, uses mad for anger chiefly in informal American speech, and builds compounds such as mad cow and mad rush.
items.cn: 现代英语保留医学义项，「生气」义主要用于非正式美式口语，并造出疯牛病、疯狂冲刺一类复合词。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers derivatives, a compound and one word that merely shares the spelling; the near group gathers words for a disturbed mind and for anger.
note.cn: 形近组收派生词、一个复合词，以及一个只是拼写相近的词；近义组收表示心智失常与愤怒的词。

entries.definition: The state of being insane, or wildly foolish behaviour.
entries.definitionCN: 精神失常的状态；疯狂的行为；由 mad 加 -ness 构成。

entries.definition: In a wild or frantic way, and informally very much.
entries.definitionCN: 疯狂地；非正式口语中作「极其」；由 mad 加 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: A man who is insane or acts with reckless violence.
entries.definitionCN: 疯子；行为狂暴失去理智的男人；由 mad 与 man 复合。

entries.definition: A polite form of address to a woman; only the spelling is close, the origin is French and unrelated.
entries.definitionCN: 对女性的礼貌称呼；与 mad 只是拼写相近，词源来自法语，二者无关。

entries.definition: Wildly unreasonable or insane, in informal use.
entries.definitionCN: 非正式用法中指极不理智或精神失常的。

entries.definition: Seriously mentally ill, or utterly foolish.
entries.definitionCN: 患严重精神病的；也指极其荒唐的。

entries.definition: Extremely angry.
entries.definitionCN: 极其愤怒的。

entries.definition: Feeling strong displeasure about something.
entries.definitionCN: 因某事而感到强烈不快的。

normalIntro.en: The word is an Old English name for a mind out of order, and its family keeps returning to illness, temper and the passions that overrule caution.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是古英语给「失序的心智」起的名字，它的同族词反复回到疾病、脾气，以及压过谨慎的激情。

normal.en: Old English already had gemǣd for foolish and insane, and modern mad is that word with its prefix worn away.
normal.cn: 古英语已有 gemǣd 表示愚蠢与精神失常，现代 mad 就是磨掉了前缀的那个词。

normal.en: The Old English prefix ge- often marks a completed state, so gemǣd pictured a mind that had been changed into something else.
normal.cn: 古英语前缀 ge- 常标记一种已完成的状态，所以 gemǣd 画出的是被改换成了别样东西的心智。

normal.en: Three ordinary endings carry the family: -ness makes madness, -ly makes madly, and man makes madman.

normal.en: Mad for anger is normal in American speech, while British speakers generally say angry instead.
normal.cn: 用 mad 表示生气在美式口语里很自然，英国人一般还是说 angry。

normal.en: To be mad about a hobby means far more than liking it: the hobby has taken over the weekends.
normal.cn: 对一项嗜好 mad about，远不只是「喜欢」：那项嗜好已经占满了周末。

abstract.en: A mind knocked out of place, like a clock whose hands have been bent by a blow.
abstract.cn: 一颗被撞离原位的心，就像一只被一击打歪了指针的钟。

abstract.en: Illness, anger and passion share one word because all three are states that take over the will.
abstract.cn: 疾病、愤怒与激情共用一个词，因为这三者都是接管了意志的状态。

abstract.en: Mad is what English says when reason has let go of the steering wheel.
abstract.cn: 当理智松开方向盘时，英语就说 mad。

examples.en: The old man had been declared mad and could no longer live alone.
examples.cn: 那位老人已被判定精神失常，再也不能独自生活。

examples.en: She was mad at me for forgetting her birthday.
examples.cn: 她因为我不记得她的生日而生我的气。

examples.en: Many drivers go mad in the city's evening traffic.

senses.title: Supernatural power used to change events
senses.definition: the supposed power to make things happen by charms, spells or secret forces beyond nature
senses.definitionCN: 通过咒语、符咒或超自然隐秘力量左右事物的、被认为存在的能力
senses.example: The villagers believed that a curse could be lifted by magic.
senses.exampleCN: 村民们相信那道咒语可以靠魔法解除。
senses.why: Greek magos named a Persian priest who read the stars, and the craft of such a priest became the ordinary word for power over events that nature does not explain.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 magos 指波斯的占星祭司，这类祭司的技艺后来成了「支配自然无法解释之事的力量」的日常说法。

senses.title: Conjuring tricks performed on stage
senses.definition: the art of producing baffling effects by sleight of hand, hidden props and misdirection
senses.definitionCN: 依靠手上功夫、暗藏道具与转移注意，制造出令人困惑效果的行当
senses.example: Her act mixed quick card magic with a dove that vanished from a hat.
senses.exampleCN: 她的节目把快速的纸牌魔术和一只从帽子里消失的鸽子混在一起。
senses.why: A stage performer copies the effects the old craft claimed, so the same noun now names a trick that everyone knows is a trick.
senses.whyCN: 舞台艺人复制了古老技艺号称能做到的效果，于是同一个名词如今指一场人人都知道是假的戏法。

senses.title: A compelling, unexplained charm
senses.definition: a quality in a place, person or moment that seems to work on people beyond ordinary cause
senses.definitionCN: 某地、某人或某一刻身上那种仿佛超出常理、能打动人的特质
senses.example: There is a certain magic in the old market at dusk.
senses.exampleCN: 黄昏时分的旧集市有一种说不清的魔力。
senses.why: If magic means power that acts without visible cause, then a place that moves people without explanation can simply be said to have magic in it.
senses.whyCN: 如果 magic 指没有可见原因就起作用的力量，那么一个说不清为何打动人的地方，自然就可以说身上带着魔力。

senses.title: Wonderful and enchanting, as an adjective
senses.definition: used beside a noun for something that seems to work beyond ordinary means or feels enchanting
senses.definitionCN: 放在名词旁边，形容某物仿佛以超乎常理的方式奏效，或令人觉得着迷
senses.example: The garden looked magic under the first snow of winter.
senses.exampleCN: 初雪落下时，那座园子看起来像被施了魔法。
senses.why: Once the noun names a power that changes things, placing it beside another noun turns it into a plain adjective for the effect.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个名词指一种改变事物的力量，把它放到另一个名词旁边，就自然变成了描述那种效果的形容词。

intro.en: Magic is a word borrowed from the title of a foreign priesthood; it then split into a claimed supernatural art, a harmless stage act, a felt charm and a plain adjective.
intro.cn: magic 是从一个外来祭司称号借来的词；它后来分成号称的超自然技艺、人畜无害的舞台戏法、可感觉得到的魅力，以及一个普通形容词。

items.en: The word is generally traced to Old Persian maguš, a member of a priestly class who read the stars and performed rites.
items.cn: 一般认为这个词可追到古波斯语 maguš，指主持仪式、观测星象的祭司阶层成员。

items.en: Greek adopted the title as magos for a Persian priest or a wandering wise man, and the abstract craft was called magikē.
items.cn: 希腊语把这个称号借作 magos，指波斯祭司或游走的智者，而那种抽象的技艺被称为 magikē。

items.en: Latin took the Greek adjective as magicus, and the related noun named the art itself rather than the man.
items.cn: 拉丁语把这个希腊形容词借作 magicus，相关的名词则指那门技艺本身，而不是那个人。

items.en: Old French magique carried noun and adjective into medieval Europe, and English borrowed the forms in the thirteenth and fourteenth centuries.
items.cn: 古法语 magique 把名词与形容词一起带进中世纪的欧洲，英语在十三、十四世纪借入这些形式。

items.en: Modern English keeps magic for the occult art and for the stage act, adds the figurative charm, and uses the bare noun before other nouns as an adjective.
items.cn: 现代英语保留 magic 指神秘技艺与舞台表演，加上比喻性的魅力，并把光秃秃的名词放在其他名词前当形容词用。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers derivatives and the biblical plural of the priestly title; the near group gathers other words for magic arts and for tricks of the senses.
note.cn: 形近组收派生词与那个祭司称号的圣经复数；近义组收其他表示法术以及感官幻象的词。

normalIntro.en: The word begins as the title of a foreign priest, and its family keeps returning to hidden knowledge, stage deception and the charm that needs no explanation.

normal.en: Latin magicus and Old French magique carried the word to English, which shortened the ending to magic.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 magicus 与古法语 magique 把词带到英语，英语把词尾缩短成 magic。

normal.en: Magician adds -ian to name the person, magical adds -al for the quality, and magically adds -ly for the manner.
normal.cn: magician 加 -ian 指人，magical 加 -al 指性质，magically 再加 -ly 指方式。

normal.en: A magic wand and a magic trick keep the stage sense, while black magic keeps the darker ritual sense.
normal.cn: magic wand 与 magic trick 守住舞台义，black magic 守住了更阴暗的仪式义。

normal.en: The adjective use grew by putting the noun before another noun, as in a magic spell or a magic touch.

abstract.en: The same word covers a trick you can learn and a power you can only imagine.

dict_mnemonic.text: 「马吉克」——马戏团里的吉克一挥手就变出鸽子；记住 magic 是魔术，也是魔法。

root: 希腊语 magos（波斯的祭司、占星师）→ 希腊语 magikē（祭司的技艺）→ 拉丁语 magicus → 古法语 magique → 英语 magic；一般认为可追到古波斯语 maguš。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a power that acts without visible cause; the senses then divide into the claimed occult art, the stage trick that copies it, a felt charm and an everyday adjective.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一种没有可见原因就起作用的力量；义项由此分成号称的神秘技艺、复制它的舞台戏法、可感觉得到的魅力，以及日常形容词。

core.cn: 核心意象：一顶高礼帽、一根细棒，白鸽从空空的袖口里扑棱飞出。

intro.en: A Persian priestly title, its Greek and Latin forms, one French borrowing and three English endings carry magic from a foreign caste to the stage and to a feeling in a place.
intro.cn: 一个波斯的祭司称号、它的希腊语与拉丁语形式、一次法语借入，再加三个英语词尾，把 magic 从外来的祭司阶层带到舞台与一个地方的氛围。

latinIntro.en: The Latin forms magicus and magus are recorded, and both descend from Greek magos, which in turn is generally traced to Old Persian maguš.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语形式 magicus 与 magus 均有记录，二者都出自希腊语 magos，而后者一般认为可追到古波斯语 maguš。

definition_zh: 磁铁；磁石；有吸引力的人或地方
definition_en: an object that attracts iron and produces a magnetic field, or a person or place that draws others
core_image: 一块黑亮的石头压在铁钉堆上，钉子像树枝一样从它身上长出来
scene: 厨房里，孩子把一张画纸吸在冰箱门上，纸没有掉下来，门上还挂着一串回形针。A small magnet holds the drawing while the fridge door swings open.
sceneCN: 这里 magnet 指「能吸铁的磁体」（第 2 个义项：人造的小块磁铁）；句意为一块小磁铁吸住画纸，冰箱门打开时纸也没掉。图中可辨识物件：冰箱门、画纸、彩色磁贴、回形针；对应第 1 个义项。

senses.title: The natural stone
senses.definition: a piece of naturally magnetized iron ore that attracts iron
senses.definitionCN: 天然带磁性的铁矿石，能吸铁
senses.example: The old compass held a sliver of magnet cut from native ore.
senses.exampleCN: 那只旧罗盘里装着一小片从天然矿石上切下来的磁石。
senses.why: Before manufacture, the word meant the ore itself: a stone found already able to move iron.
senses.whyCN: 在人工制造出现之前，这个词指的就是矿石本身：一块被发现时就已经能移动铁的石头。

senses.title: A shaped piece of magnetized metal
senses.titleCN: 人造磁铁：加工成形的磁体
senses.definition: a piece of metal or ceramic made so that it attracts iron
senses.definitionCN: 经过加工、能吸铁的金属或陶瓷块
senses.example: He stuck the note to the fridge with a small magnet.
senses.exampleCN: 他用一块小磁铁把便条贴在冰箱上。
senses.why: The same power found in ore can be shaped into bars and discs, so the noun widened from a found stone to a made tool.
senses.whyCN: 矿石里的那种力量可以被加工成条块与圆片，于是这个名词从捡到的石头扩大到做出来的工具。

senses.title: A coil with an iron core
senses.titleCN: 电磁铁：靠电流工作的磁体
senses.definition: a coil of wire with an iron core that acts as a magnet while current flows
senses.definitionCN: 通电时起磁体作用的带铁芯线圈
senses.example: The crane's magnet releases the scrap metal when the current stops.
senses.exampleCN: 电流一断，吊车的电磁铁就把废金属放开。
senses.why: Once electricity could make magnetism, a magnet no longer had to be a permanent stone; it could be switched on and off.
senses.whyCN: 当电能够制造磁性，磁体就不必再是永久的石头，而可以被开与关。

senses.title: The two poles of a magnet
senses.definition: one of the two ends of a magnet, where the pull is strongest and opposite poles attract
senses.definitionCN: 磁体两端吸力最强之处，异极相吸、同极相斥
senses.example: Every magnet has a north pole and a south pole, however often it is cut.
senses.exampleCN: 无论把磁铁切多少次，每一块都仍有南极和北极。
senses.why: The object is not uniform: the pull concentrates at the ends, and that pair of ends is part of what the word names.
senses.whyCN: 物体并不均匀：吸力集中在两端，而这一对端点也是这个词所指内容的一部分。

senses.title: A charming person
senses.definition: a person who attracts others strongly, as if by magnetism
senses.definitionCN: 像被磁力吸引那样强烈吸引他人的人
senses.example: As a speaker she was a magnet, and the hall filled within minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 作为演讲者，她像一块磁石，几分钟就把礼堂填满了。
senses.why: A stone that draws iron is an easy picture for a person who draws a crowd, so the noun moved from metal to people.
senses.whyCN: 吸铁的石头很容易拿来比喻吸住人群的人，于是这个名词从金属转到了人。

senses.title: A place that draws visitors
senses.definition: a place that attracts many visitors or residents
senses.definitionCN: 吸引大量游客或居民的地方
senses.example: The rebuilt pier became a magnet for day trippers.
senses.exampleCN: 重建后的码头成了当日游客的聚集地。
senses.why: A place pulls people the way the stone pulls iron: no one orders the crowd to come, yet the current of visitors bends toward it.
senses.whyCN: 地方吸人就像磁石吸铁：没有人下令，游客的人流却朝它弯过去。

senses.title: A centre that draws resources
senses.titleCN: 吸引人才与资金的中心
senses.definition: an institution or district that draws talent, money or investment
senses.definitionCN: 吸引人才、资金或投资的机构或地区
senses.example: The research park is a magnet for young engineers.
senses.exampleCN: 这座研究园区是年轻工程师的聚集地。
senses.why: The metaphor turns practical: a place that offers work and equipment draws skilled people and their money as reliably as a field draws iron.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻转为实用：一个提供工作与设备的地方，吸来技术人才与资金，其可靠程度如同磁场吸铁。

senses.title: Anything that captures attention
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：吸引注意力的事物
senses.definition: anything that holds attention so firmly that people turn to it
senses.definitionCN: 牢牢抓住注意力、让人转向它的事物
senses.example: That question acted as a magnet for the whole debate.
senses.exampleCN: 那个问题像磁石一样吸住了整场辩论。
senses.why: The pull can attach to nothing physical at all: an idea holds attention the way a stone holds filings, and the noun needs no metal.
senses.whyCN: 这种拉力完全可以不附着在任何实物上：一个念头抓住注意，就像石头抓住铁屑，这个名词不再需要金属。

intro.en: Magnet comes from the Greek name of the stone of Magnesia through Latin and Old French. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: magnet 经拉丁语与古法语，上溯希腊语中「马格尼西亚的石头」之名。年代均为约数。

items.en: Magnētis lithos, the stone of Magnesia, named a natural iron ore that already attracted iron. The place-name account is generally accepted; the origin of the place name is not settled.
items.cn: magnētis lithos 即「马格尼西亚的石头」，指一种本身就能吸铁的天然矿石。以地名解释这一石名一般认为是可行的；地名本身的来源没有定论。

items.en: Latin took the Greek noun as magnes, genitive magnetis, and used it for the ore and for anything that behaved like it.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入该希腊名词作 magnes，属格 magnetis，既指矿石，也指任何行为像它的东西。

items.en: Old French magnete carried the word into English in the thirteenth century, at first as the name of the mineral.
items.cn: 古法语 magnete 在十三世纪把这个词带进英语，最初是矿物的名字。

items.en: Experimenters began shaping iron into artificial magnets, and the word widened from a found stone to any made object with the same power.
items.cn: 实验者开始把铁加工成人造磁体，这个词也从「捡到的石头」扩大到任何具有同样力量的制成品。

items.en: In 1825 William Sturgeon wrapped a coil around an iron core and called it an electromagnet, tying the noun to a switchable device.
items.cn: 1825 年斯特金把线圈绕在铁芯上，称之为电磁铁，把这个名词与可开关的装置绑在一起。

items.en: By the nineteenth and twentieth centuries a magnet was also a person or place that draws others, especially visitors, talent or money.
items.cn: 到十九、二十世纪，magnet 也指吸引他人的人或地方，尤其吸引游客、人才或资金。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the same stem and one look-alike from another root; group two holds things that attract in the same practical way.
note.cn: 第一组是同出该词干的词，以及一个异源形近词；第二组是在实际用途上同样能吸引东西的事物。

entries.definition: Describes what a magnet is or does; the noun names the object.
entries.definitionCN: 形容磁体是什么、能做什么；名词则指物件。

entries.definition: The property or the science; a magnet is the thing that has it.
entries.definitionCN: 性质或学科；magnet 是拥有这一性质的东西。

entries.definition: The black mineral that magnets are made from and that occurs naturally magnetized.
entries.definitionCN: 可用来制作磁体、也会天然带磁的黑色矿物。

entries.definition: A business magnate, from Latin magnus 'great'; it is not related to the stone at all.
entries.definitionCN: 商业巨头，来自拉丁 magnus「大的」；与磁石毫无同源关系。

entries.definition: The old name for naturally magnetized magnetite, the original magnet.
entries.definitionCN: 天然带磁的磁铁矿的旧称，也就是最早的磁石。

entries.definition: A magnet that works only while current flows, so it can be turned off.
entries.definitionCN: 只在通电时起作用的磁体，因此可以关掉。

entries.definition: Any drawing force; a magnet is one physical source of it.
entries.definitionCN: 任何拉力；磁体是它在物理上的一种来源。

entries.definition: The act of pulling a crowd or interest; a magnet is the object that produces the draw.
entries.definitionCN: 吸引人群或兴趣的动作；magnet 是产生这种吸引的物件。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real stone name, the real compounds and the real modern metaphors.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的石名、真实的复合词，以及真实存在的现代比喻。

normal.en: The word is the stone, not the property: magnet names the thing, magnetism names what it has.
normal.cn: 这个词指的是石头而非性质：magnet 指物件，magnetism 指它拥有的东西。

normal.en: Everyday magnets carry prefixes: electromagnet, nanomagnet, fridge magnet.
normal.cn: 日常磁体常带前缀：电磁铁、纳米磁体、冰箱贴。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the figurative sense: a magnet for tourists, a magnet for talent, a magnet school.
normal.cn: 固定搭配显示比喻义：吸引游客的地方、吸引人才的中心、特色择优学校。

normal.en: The same stone name gives magnetite, the ore, and magnetometer, the measuring device.
normal.cn: 同一个石名还给出 magnetite（矿石）与 magnetometer（测量器械）。

normal.en: Cut a magnet in half and you do not get one pole; you get two smaller magnets, each with both poles.
normal.cn: 把磁铁切成两半，你不会得到一个单极，而是得到两块更小的磁铁，各有两极。

abstract.en: Picture a stone that grows iron branches when it is laid on a pile of nails.
abstract.cn: 想象一块石头放在钉堆上，就长出铁的枝条。

abstract.en: Picture a switch that turns attraction on and off without moving the metal.
abstract.cn: 想象一个开关，不动金属就能让吸引力出现或消失。

abstract.en: Picture a town where every road seems to slope gently toward the same square.
abstract.cn: 想象一座小镇，每条路都像微微向下倾向同一个广场。

examples.en: A magnet is useless once it is heated far above its working temperature.
examples.cn: 磁铁被加热到远超工作温度之后就没用了。

examples.en: The festival has become a magnet for young filmmakers.
examples.cn: 这个影展已经成了年轻电影人的聚集地。

examples.en: She kept the spare key under a magnet on the steel door.
examples.cn: 她把备用钥匙放在钢门上的磁贴下面。

dict_mnemonic.text: 马格内特——来自马格尼西亚的石头，能吸铁 → 磁石、磁铁

root: 希腊 magnētis lithos（马格尼西亚石）→ 拉丁 magnes/magnetis → 古法语 magnete → 英语 magnet。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses begin with the native ore and the shaped object, then its poles and its electric version, and end with the person, place and idea that draw others.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从天然矿石与成形磁体出发，经过两极与电磁版本，最后落到吸人的人、地方与念头。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a black stone with iron nails growing out of it like branches.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块黑石头上长出铁钉，像树枝一样。

branches.en: Found stone and made object: the same power, first in ore and then in a shaped piece.
branches.cn: 捡来的石头与制成的物件：同一种力量，先在矿石里，后在成形块里。

branches.en: A magnet can be switched by current, and every version still has two poles.
branches.cn: 磁体可由电流开关，而无论哪种版本都仍有两极。

branches.en: The stone's pull applied to a person who holds a room.
branches.cn: 磁石的拉力用在一个人身上，他能稳住一屋子人。

branches.en: A place or an institution that pulls visitors, talent and money.
branches.cn: 一个地方或机构，吸来游客、人才与资金。

branches.en: The pull detached from place and metal, working on attention itself.
branches.cn: 拉力脱离地方与金属，直接作用于注意力。

intro.en: Magnet is a free noun from Greek through Latin, and all its relatives attach ordinary suffixes to that stem.
intro.cn: magnet 是经拉丁语来自希腊语的自由名词，所有亲属词都在这同一词干上加普通后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin magnes, genitive magnetis, is the direct source; magnetismus is a New Latin extension, and Greek magnēs stands at the head of the chain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 magnes（属格 magnetis）是直接来源；magnetismus 是新拉丁语的延伸，链条最前端是希腊 magnēs。

items.example: The magnet clung to the steel frame.
items.exampleCN: 磁铁吸在钢架上。

items.meaning: having the power of a magnet
items.meaningCN: 有磁性的（加形容词后缀，物件转为性质）
items.example: The magnetic clamp held the plate.
items.exampleCN: 磁性夹具固定住板块。

items.meaningCN: 磁性（加状态后缀，物件转为性质）
items.example: Magnetism faded as the metal cooled.
items.exampleCN: 金属冷却后磁性减弱。

items.meaning: to make an object act like a magnet
items.meaningCN: 使磁化（加使动后缀，性质被赋予别的物件）
items.example: A brief pulse magnetizes the needle.
items.exampleCN: 一次短脉冲就能使指针磁化。

items.meaning: the process or strength of being magnetized
items.meaningCN: 磁化过程或磁化强度（再加过程后缀）
items.example: The magnetization survived the drop.
items.exampleCN: 跌落之后磁化状态仍在。

items.meaning: the black ore that magnets occur in
items.meaningCN: 磁铁矿（加矿物后缀，由物件转为矿种）
items.example: Magnetite grains darken the sand.
items.exampleCN: 磁铁矿颗粒把沙子染黑。

items.meaning: a magnet driven by a coil
items.meaningCN: 电磁铁（电加磁体，动力来源变成电流）
items.example: The electromagnet lifts the car bodies.
items.exampleCN: 电磁铁把车身吊起。

items.meaning: a small decorative magnet for a refrigerator
items.meaningCN: 冰箱贴（由冰箱与磁体复合，用途收窄到装饰）
items.example: She bought a fridge magnet at the museum.
items.exampleCN: 她在博物馆买了一个冰箱贴。

definition_zh: 有磁性的；磁的；靠磁力驱动的；有强烈吸引力的
definition_en: having the power to attract iron, or relating to magnets, magnetic fields and the force they produce
core_image: 一块黑色矿石隔着白纸把铁屑排成一道道弧线，纸下什么都没有，铁屑却自己排队
scene: 实验室的白纸上，一块黑色矿石压着薄薄一层铁屑，铁屑自己排成弧线，围观的人都屏住了呼吸。A magnetic mineral draws iron filings into curved lines even through a sheet of paper.
sceneCN: 这里 magnetic 指「具有吸引铁、能产生磁场的性质」（第 1 个义项：能够吸引铁并形成磁场）；句意为一块有磁性的矿石隔着白纸也能把铁屑吸成弧线。图中可辨识物件：黑色矿石、白纸、铁屑、放大镜；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 有磁性的；磁的；靠磁力工作的

senses.title: Attracting iron
senses.definition: having the property of attracting iron and producing a magnetic field around itself
senses.definitionCN: 具有吸引铁并在周围产生磁场的性质
senses.example: A magnetic rod lifted every nail from the bench in one sweep.
senses.exampleCN: 一根有磁性的棒子一扫，就把工作台上的钉子全吸了起来。
senses.why: The word names the property that first made a certain ore famous: iron moves toward it although nothing visible pulls.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名的是让某种矿石最早出名的性质：看不见任何东西在拉，铁却朝它移动。

senses.title: Belonging to the study of magnets
senses.titleCN: 与磁学、磁力研究有关的
senses.definition: relating to magnetism as a subject of scientific study
senses.definitionCN: 与作为科学研究对象的磁学、磁力有关
senses.example: Her thesis examines the magnetic behaviour of thin films.
senses.exampleCN: 她的论文研究薄膜的磁性行为。
senses.why: Once the stone became an object of experiment, the adjective shifted from the object to the whole field of inquiry.
senses.whyCN: 当磁石成为实验对象之后，这个形容词就从物件本身转到了整个研究领域。

senses.title: Driven by magnetic force
senses.definition: operated or produced by magnetic forces rather than by direct contact
senses.definitionCN: 靠磁力而非直接接触来运转或产生
senses.example: The magnetic levitation train floats above its guideway.
senses.exampleCN: 磁悬浮列车悬浮在导轨上方。
senses.why: If a stone can move iron without touching it, that pull can also be harnessed to lift a whole train.
senses.whyCN: 既然磁石不接触就能移动铁，这股拉力自然也就能用来托起整列火车。

senses.title: Of a planet's field
senses.definition: relating to the natural field generated by a planet or a star
senses.definitionCN: 与行星或恒星自然产生的磁场有关
senses.example: Migrating birds appear to read the magnetic field of the earth.
senses.exampleCN: 迁徙的鸟似乎能读取地球的磁场。
senses.why: The same invisible influence surrounds the whole planet, so the adjective applies to fields far larger than any stone.
senses.whyCN: 同一种看不见的作用笼罩整个行星，于是这个词也用于比任何磁石都大得多的场。

senses.title: Storing data in magnetized material
senses.definition: using magnetized material to record and keep information
senses.definitionCN: 用被磁化的材料记录并保存信息
senses.example: The old magnetic tape still holds the studio recordings.
senses.exampleCN: 那卷旧磁带里还存着当年的录音。
senses.why: A magnet can fix a pattern in iron particles, and a fixed pattern can carry a signal, so magnetism became a way to write memory.
senses.whyCN: 磁体能在铁微粒里固定下一道图案，而固定图案可以承载信号，于是磁性成了写入记忆的手段。

senses.title: Having two opposite poles
senses.titleCN: 分南北极、同极相斥异极相吸
senses.definition: having north and south poles that attract and repel one another
senses.definitionCN: 具有南北两极，同极相斥、异极相吸
senses.example: Two magnetic poles of the same kind push each other away.
senses.exampleCN: 两个同类的磁极会把对方推开。
senses.why: The pull is never single: it always comes in a pair of opposite ends, which is why the adjective also describes polarity.
senses.whyCN: 这种拉力从不单独出现，总是成对的两端，因此这个词也用来描述极性。

senses.title: Charming a room
senses.definition: having a personality that draws people strongly and willingly
senses.definitionCN: 具有让人不由自主被吸引的个性
senses.example: Her magnetic presence made the whole room quiet.
senses.exampleCN: 她那种有磁性的气场让整个房间安静下来。
senses.why: The metaphor borrows the stone's invisible pull: nothing is said or forced, yet attention turns toward the person.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻借用了磁石看不见的拉力：没有言语也没有强迫，注意力却转向那个人。

senses.title: An abstract pull
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：不可抗拒的吸引力
senses.definition: exerting an attraction so strong that it feels physical
senses.definitionCN: 施加一种强到近乎物理层面的吸引
senses.example: The magnetic appeal of the old city keeps artists returning.
senses.exampleCN: 老城那种不可抗拒的吸引力让艺术家一再回来。
senses.why: The abstract sense generalizes the stone: what is attracted is no longer iron but a person, a memory or a whole crowd.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义把磁石一般化：被吸引的不再是铁，而是人、记忆或一整群人。

intro.en: Magnetic goes back to the Greek name of a stone from Magnesia, through Latin magnes and the later Latin adjective magneticus. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: magnetic 经拉丁 magnes 与晚期拉丁形容词 magneticus，上溯希腊语中一种来自马格尼西亚的石头之名。年代均为约数。

items.en: Magnētis lithos, 'the stone of Magnesia', named a naturally magnetized iron ore. The place-name explanation is generally accepted, but the origin of the place name itself is not settled.
items.cn: magnētis lithos 意为「马格尼西亚的石头」，指一种天然带磁性的铁矿石。以地名解释这一石名一般认为是可行的，但地名本身的来源没有定论。

items.en: Latin borrowed the Greek noun as magnes, genitive magnetis, and later formed the adjective magneticus from the same stem.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入这个希腊名词，作 magnes，属格 magnetis；后来又用同一词干构成形容词 magneticus。

items.en: English magnet is recorded in the thirteenth century through Old French magnete, and the adjective magnetic follows in the sixteenth.
items.cn: 英语 magnet 在十三世纪经古法语 magnete 出现，形容词 magnetic 则到十六世纪才跟上。

items.en: From the sixteenth century magnetic described the invisible influence itself, and magnetic field became standard after Faraday's experiments in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 从十六世纪起，magnetic 开始描述那种看不见的作用本身；到十九世纪法拉第的实验之后，magnetic field 成为标准说法。

items.en: Animal magnetism, the theory Franz Mesmer promoted in the 1770s, supplied the metaphor of a person who draws others like iron to a lodestone.
items.cn: 梅斯默在十八世纪七十年代推崇的「动物磁力」理论，提供了「人像铁被磁石吸引」这一比喻。

items.en: Source uncertain (place name and first record): the link to Magnesia is generally accepted, yet the origin of the place name and the exact earliest English citation of magnetic remain unsettled.
items.cn: 来源不确定（地名与首见记录）：与马格尼西亚的联系一般认为是成立的，但地名的来源以及 magnetic 最早的确切英语书证仍无定论。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the same magnet stem, plus one look-alike from a different root; group two holds words for the pull itself.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 magnet 词干的词，另加一个形近却异源的词；第二组是表示「吸引力」本身的词。

entries.definition: The stone or device itself; magnetic is the adjective made from it.
entries.definitionCN: 磁石或磁体本身；magnetic 是由它构成的形容词。

entries.definition: The property or the science, not the object; the ending -ism marks a state or system.
entries.definitionCN: 指性质或学科，而不是物件；-ism 后缀标记状态或体系。

entries.definition: The black iron ore that can be magnetized; the ending -ite marks a mineral.
entries.definitionCN: 能被磁化的黑色铁矿石；-ite 后缀标记矿物。

entries.definition: A powerful person in business or industry, from Latin magnus 'great'; it shares spelling only, not ancestry.
entries.definitionCN: 商业或工业界的权贵，来自拉丁 magnus「大的」；只同拼写，并不同源。

entries.definition: Pleasing enough to draw interest, used of looks or offers; it carries no hint of a field.
entries.definitionCN: 足够讨喜而引来兴趣，多用于外貌或条件；不含磁场的意味。

entries.definition: Able to inspire followers through force of personality; narrower than magnetic and mainly about leaders.
entries.definitionCN: 靠人格力量鼓舞追随者；比 magnetic 窄，主要用于领袖。

entries.definition: Attractive in a way that promises pleasure or gain; it suggests enticement rather than natural pull.
entries.definitionCN: 以快乐或利益诱人的；偏「引诱」而非自然吸引。

entries.definition: So absorbing that attention cannot leave it; stronger and stranger than magnetic.
entries.definitionCN: 吸引人到无法移开注意；比 magnetic 更强也更奇异。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real stem, the real compounds and the real phrases of the magnet family.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的词干、真实的复合词，以及磁石词族里真实存在的搭配。

normal.en: The stem is the name of a stone from Magnesia, so magnet came before magnetism and magnetic.
normal.cn: 词干来自马格尼西亚的一种石头之名，因此先有 magnet，才有 magnetism 与 magnetic。

normal.en: The family runs magnet, magnetism, magnetize, magnetite, electromagnet and magnetometer.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 magnet、magnetism、magnetize、magnetite、electromagnet 与 magnetometer。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the physical sense: magnetic field, magnetic pole, magnetic force, magnetic compass.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出物理义：磁场、磁极、磁力、磁罗盘。

normal.en: The same adjective serves the metaphor: a magnetic personality draws people the way a stone draws pins.
normal.cn: 同一个形容词也承担比喻：有魅力的个性吸人，正如磁石吸针。

normal.en: Electricity and magnetism sit side by side: electromagnet joins electro- to magnet.
normal.cn: 电与磁并肩而立：electromagnet 由 electro- 与 magnet 拼成。

abstract.en: Picture an invisible hand under the paper: the filings line up though nothing touches them.
abstract.cn: 想象纸下有一只无形的手：没有东西碰到铁屑，它们却排好了队。

abstract.en: Picture two ends that cannot be separated: cut the bar in half and each half still has a north and a south.
abstract.cn: 想象两个无法分开的端点：把磁条切成两半，每一半仍有南极和北极。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd drifting toward one speaker without being told to move.
abstract.cn: 想象一群人没有接到任何指令，却慢慢朝同一个演讲者靠过去。

examples.en: The magnetic strip on the card was worn, so the machine could not read it.
examples.cn: 卡片上的磁条磨损了，机器读不出来。

examples.en: Iron is strongly magnetic, while copper barely responds at all.
examples.cn: 铁有很强的磁性，而铜几乎毫无反应。

examples.en: The campaign gained magnetic force once the young mayor joined it.
examples.cn: 年轻市长加入之后，这场运动有了强大的吸引力。

dict_mnemonic.text: magnet（磁石）+ -ic（形容词后缀）——像磁石那样会吸 → 有磁性的；也有吸引力

root: 希腊语 magnētis lithos（马格尼西亚的石头）→ 拉丁 magnes/magnetis → 拉丁形容词 magneticus → 英语 magnetic；地名来源一般认为是，地名本身来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses begin with a stone pulling iron, pass through field, machine and stored data, and end with the pull a person or a place exerts on a crowd.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一块吸铁的石头出发，经过磁场、机器与存储的数据，最后落到一个人或一个地方对人群的吸引力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stone moves iron across a sheet of paper without ever touching it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块石头隔着纸移动铁，却从不接触它。

branches.en: The stone and its poles: attraction and repulsion are two faces of one property.
branches.cn: 磁石与其两极：吸与斥是同一种性质的两张脸。

branches.en: From property to force: what the physicist measures is what the machine harnesses.
branches.cn: 从性质到力：物理学家测量的，正是机器所利用的。

branches.en: The planet itself as one huge magnet with a field around it.
branches.cn: 行星本身就是一块巨大的磁铁，外面罩着一层场。

branches.en: The pull fixed into matter as a pattern that can be read back.
branches.cn: 把拉力固定进物质，变成可以读回的图案。

branches.en: The same pull felt between people, or toward a place or an idea.
branches.cn: 同样的拉力发生在人与人之间，或指向一个地方、一个念头。

intro.en: Magnetic is an adjective built on the noun magnet with the Latin suffix -ic, so the whole family reads outward from the stone.
intro.cn: magnetic 是名词 magnet 加拉丁形容词后缀 -ic 构成，整个词族都可以从磁石向外读。

latinIntro.en: Latin magnes, genitive magnetis, came from Greek magnēs; New Latin added magnetismus for the property, and English built the rest on that stem.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 magnes（属格 magnetis）来自希腊 magnēs；新拉丁语又加 magnetismus 表示性质，英语其余词都建在这个词干上。

items.meaning: a stone or device that attracts iron
items.example: The magnet held the note to the steel door.
items.exampleCN: 磁铁把便条吸在钢门上。

items.meaning: of a magnet; able to attract
items.meaningCN: 磁的；有吸引力的（加形容词后缀，由物件转为性质）
items.example: The magnetic field bends the beam.
items.exampleCN: 磁场使电子束偏转。

items.meaning: the property of magnets; the science of it
items.meaningCN: 磁性；磁学（加状态后缀，由物件转为性质与学科）
items.example: Magnetism puzzled naturalists for centuries.
items.exampleCN: 磁性感住了博物学家好几个世纪。

items.meaningCN: 使磁化（加动词后缀，表示使成为）
items.example: The current magnetizes the iron core.
items.exampleCN: 电流使铁芯磁化。

items.meaning: the process or degree of becoming magnetic
items.meaningCN: 磁化过程或磁化程度（再加名词后缀，表示过程与结果）
items.example: Magnetization reverses as the current alternates.
items.exampleCN: 电流交变时，磁化方向随之反转。

items.meaning: the black iron ore that magnets occur in
items.meaningCN: 磁铁矿（加矿物后缀，由性质转到具体矿石）
items.example: Magnetite lies in bands along the ridge.
items.exampleCN: 磁铁矿沿着山脊成带状分布。

items.meaning: a magnet worked by an electric coil
items.meaningCN: 电磁铁（由「电」与人造磁体复合，动力来源改变）
items.example: The electromagnet drops the load when switched off.
items.exampleCN: 断电时电磁铁把货物放下。

items.meaning: an instrument for measuring magnetic strength
items.meaningCN: 磁强计（加测量器械后缀，由性质转为量具）
items.example: The survey used a magnetometer over the wreck.
items.exampleCN: 勘测时用磁强计扫过沉船。

items.meaningCN: 非磁性的（加否定前缀，性质被取消）
items.example: The case is made of nonmagnetic steel.
items.exampleCN: 外壳用的是非磁性钢。

latinEntries.meaning: the region that gave the stone its name
latinEntries.meaningCN: 给这种石头命名的那一地区

definition_zh: 宏伟的；壮丽的；极好的；出色的；慷慨的；气魄宏大的
definition_en: impressively large and beautiful, excellent of its kind, generous on a grand scale, or noble in spirit
core_image: 一座巨大的穹顶压在石柱之上，让人抬头时不自觉放慢脚步
scene: 黄昏时分，游客站在广场尽头，抬头看那座穹顶，石阶上还留着白天的余温。The magnificent dome caught the last light and seemed to lift the whole square.
sceneCN: 这里 magnificent 是「宏伟的、壮丽的」（第 1 个义项：规模与形制令人震动）；句意为那座宏伟的穹顶接住最后的天光，仿佛把整个广场托了起来。图中可辨识物件：石阶、穹顶、广场尽头的游客。

pos.zh: 宏伟的；壮丽的；极好的；慷慨的；气魄宏大的

derivatives.zh: 由 magnificent 加 -ence 构成，义为「宏伟；壮丽」
由 magnificent 加 -ly 构成，义为「宏伟地；极出色地」

senses.title: Impressively large and beautiful
senses.definition: so large and beautifully made or placed that it fills the eye and impresses the mind
senses.definitionCN: 规模巨大、形制或位置极美，足以占满视野并震动人心
senses.example: The magnificent dome caught the last light and seemed to lift the whole square.
senses.exampleCN: 那座宏伟的穹顶接住最后的天光，仿佛把整个广场都托了起来。
senses.why: Latin magnificus joined magnus, great, to -ficus, making, so the word first praises what makes its surroundings look great.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 magnificus 把意为「大」的 magnus 与意为「使……成」的 -ficus 拼在一起，所以这个词最初赞美的是让周围显得宏大的东西。

senses.title: Excellent of its kind
senses.definition: done or made to a very high standard, so that it stands out among others of its kind
senses.definitionCN: 以极高水准完成或制成，在同类之中格外突出
senses.example: She gave a magnificent performance in the final act.
senses.exampleCN: 她在最后一幕献上了一场极为出色的演出。
senses.why: Greatness is measured by effect rather than by size, so a voice or a performance that overwhelms the audience earns the same word as a building does.
senses.whyCN: 宏大与否是看效果而不是看体积，所以一副压得住全场的好嗓子、一场压得住全场的演出，能和大建筑共用同一个词。

senses.title: Generous on a grand scale
senses.definition: giving freely and in large amounts, so that the gift itself feels splendid
senses.definitionCN: 毫不吝惜地大量给予，以至于所给之物本身就显得堂皇
senses.example: The old man made a magnificent gift to the village school.
senses.exampleCN: 那位老人给村校捐了一份极为慷慨的礼物。
senses.why: Greatness turned outward becomes generosity, and a gift given without counting the cost looks as grand as any monument.
senses.whyCN: 宏大一旦朝外转，就成了慷慨；一份不计较代价送出的礼物，看上去和任何纪念碑一样气派。

senses.title: Noble and grand in spirit
senses.definition: showing a large, forgiving or courageous spirit in a moment of action
senses.definitionCN: 在行动的一刻显出宽厚、宽容或勇敢的气度
senses.example: He offered a magnificent gesture of forgiveness to the family who had wronged him.
senses.exampleCN: 他向那个曾亏待他的家庭做出了一个气魄宏大的宽恕姿态。
senses.why: If stone and sound can be magnificent, so can a choice, and the word extends from spectacle to the moral size of a person.
senses.whyCN: 既然石头与声音可以宏伟，一个选择也可以；这个词便从场面扩展到了人精神上的分量。

intro.en: Magnificent is built from two Latin pieces meaning great and making, and it reached English through French with the sense of grandeur already attached.
intro.cn: magnificent 由两个拉丁语成分拼成，分别意为「大」与「使……成」；它带着已有的「宏大」含义经法语进入英语。

items.en: Magnus was the ordinary Latin adjective for great in size, power or rank, and it stands behind a whole family of English words.
items.cn: magnus 是拉丁语中表示体积、力量或地位之「大」的普通形容词，一整族英语词都站在它背后。

items.en: The verb facere means to make or to do, and its combining form -ficus marks whatever produces or causes something.
items.cn: 动词 facere 意为「做、造」，它的构词形式 -ficus 表示「产生、造成某物」。

items.en: Magnus plus -ficus gave magnificus, literally making great, and the word described things that enlarge the scene around them.
items.cn: magnus 加 -ficus 得到 magnificus，字面意为「使……变大」，用来形容把周围景象衬托得更大的事物。

items.en: The noun magnificentia named grandeur, and the comparative magnificentior supplied the form that passed into French and then English.
items.cn: 名词 magnificentia 指宏大、壮丽，比较级 magnificentior 提供了后来经法语进入英语的那个形式。

items.en: English borrowed magnificent in the fifteenth century and now applies it to buildings, performances, gifts and acts of spirit.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪借入 magnificent，如今把它用于建筑、演出、礼物，以及精神上的举动。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers relatives built on the Latin stem for great and making; the near group gathers adjectives that also praise scale, beauty or excellence.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁语「大」与「做」这两个词干上的同族词；近义组收同样赞美规模、美感或出色的形容词。

entries.definition: The quality of being grand and splendid.
entries.definitionCN: 宏伟；壮丽；由 magnificent 加 -ence 构成。

entries.definition: In a grand or splendid manner.
entries.definitionCN: 宏伟地；极出色地；由 magnificent 加 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: To make something look larger, from the same Latin verb for making.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物看起来更大；与 magnificent 同出拉丁语中表示「做」的动词。

entries.definition: The great size or importance of something.
entries.definitionCN: 某物的巨大或重要程度；与 magnificent 共用拉丁语 magnus（大）。

entries.definition: Magnificent in appearance or very good indeed.
entries.definitionCN: 外观壮丽的；也确实非常好的。

entries.definition: Large and impressive in scale or style.
entries.definitionCN: 规模或气派上宏大而令人印象深刻的。

entries.definition: Having a dignified, royal beauty.
entries.definitionCN: 带有庄严、王者般的美感的。

entries.definition: Impressive because of size or presence.
entries.definitionCN: 因体积或气势而令人肃然起敬的。

normalIntro.en: The word joins a Latin adjective for great to a Latin verb for making, and its family keeps returning to size, splendour and actions that enlarge the people who do them.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词把拉丁语表示「大」的形容词与表示「做」的动词拼在一起，它的同族词反复回到体积、壮丽，以及让做这件事的人显得更大的举动。

normal.en: Latin magnus means great, and -ficus comes from facere, to make, so magnificent is literally making great.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 magnus 意为「大」，-ficus 出自 facere（做），所以 magnificent 字面就是「使……宏大」。

normal.en: Magnificence adds -ence for the quality, and magnificently adds -ly for the manner of doing something.
normal.cn: magnificence 加 -ence 指性质，magnificently 加 -ly 指做事的方式。

normal.en: Magnify and magnitude share the same magnus stem, so the family keeps returning to size and greatness.
normal.cn: magnify 与 magnitude 共用 magnus 这个词干，所以这个词族一直回到体积与宏大。

normal.en: The word was borrowed through French in the fifteenth century, which is why it keeps the Latin -fic- shape.
normal.cn: 这个词在十五世纪经法语借入，所以至今保留拉丁语的 -fic- 形状。

normal.en: A magnificent view praises scale and beauty, while a magnificent gift praises generosity.
normal.cn: magnificent view 赞美规模与美，magnificent gift 赞美的则是慷慨。

abstract.en: Greatness that can be seen: the word always asks the eye to widen.
abstract.cn: 一种看得见的宏大：这个词总是要求人把眼界放宽。

abstract.en: A building and a kindness can both be magnificent, because both make the world around them look larger.
abstract.cn: 一座建筑与一份善意都可以是 magnificent，因为二者都让周围的世界显得更大。

abstract.en: The word joins great to make, a reminder that grandeur is often something done rather than owned.
abstract.cn: 这个词把「大」与「做」连在一起，提醒人：气派常常是做出来的，而不是拥有的。

examples.en: The magnificent dome caught the last light and seemed to lift the whole square.
examples.cn: 那座宏伟的穹顶接住最后的天光，仿佛把整个广场都托了起来。

examples.en: She gave a magnificent performance in the final act.
examples.cn: 她在最后一幕献上了一场极为出色的演出。

examples.en: The old man made a magnificent gift to the village school.
examples.cn: 那位老人给村校捐了一份极为慷慨的礼物。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「马格尼菲森」——马戏团的大帐篷一拉开，全场都为它的宏伟惊叹；记住 magnificent 是宏伟的、极好的。

root: 拉丁语 magnus（大的）+ -ficus（做、使……，源自 facere）→ magnificus（使显得宏大的）→ magnificentia 与比较级 magnificentior → 古法语 magnificent → 英语 magnificent。

sensesIntro.en: The core is greatness made visible; the senses then divide into imposing scale, excellent quality, lavish giving and a noble spirit.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「被看见的宏大」；义项由此分成震撼的规模、极高的水准、出手阔绰的给予，以及高尚的气度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a vast dome resting on stone columns, making every visitor slow down and look up.
core.cn: 核心意象：一座巨大的穹顶压在石柱之上，让每个来访者都放慢脚步抬头看。

branches.en: a dome lifting above the rooftops
branches.cn: 穹顶高过一片屋脊

branches.en: a crowded hall breaking into applause
branches.cn: 满堂观众爆出掌声

branches.en: a soloist holding the last note
branches.cn: 独唱者拖住最后一个音

branches.en: a cheque handed to a village school
branches.cn: 一张支票交到村校

branches.en: an old man shaking hands after cancelling a debt
branches.cn: 老人免除债务后与人握手

intro.en: Two Latin stems, one for great and one for making, their Latin derivatives and two English endings carry magnificent from size to splendour and to generosity of spirit.
intro.cn: 两个拉丁词干，一个表示「大」，一个表示「做」，加上它们的拉丁派生词与两个英语词尾，把 magnificent 从体积带到壮丽，再带到精神上的慷慨。

latinIntro.en: Magnus, facere, magnificus and magnificentia are all recorded Latin words, and the English adjective descends from the same family through French.
latinIntro.cn: magnus、facere、magnificus 与 magnificentia 都是有记录的拉丁词，英语这个形容词经法语出自同一族。
